Snow Hunter comes from an offshoot of Kjerag's Clan Paleroche that went into the mountains, where they have lived as hunters for generations, passing down the craft of carving Kjeragandr sculptures.
With her experience of hunting in the snowy mountains, she demonstrates excellent athleticism. She currently receives treatment at Rhodes Island after a hunting accident left her with Oripathy, and is assigned to field missions at her own request.

Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Originium crystals are present on Operator Snow Hunter's arm.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L
Operator Snow Hunter is still developing physically. She demonstrates excellent physical abilities as a result of her active lifestyle in the mountains, but continued observation is needed to prevent deterioration of Oripathy symptoms.

[Rift Cloudbeast Health Examination Report]
The Rift Cloudbeast is in good health with no signs of Oripathy, but is slightly overweight. Consider reducing daily food intake.

With our experience in onboarding operators from different countries, plus having received a heads-up from Pramanix ahead of time, we were confident that Snow Hunter's background as a huntress in Kjerag would not present any particular difficulty, and that she would successfully integrate into Rhodes Island within a month. However, what had happened was truly unprecedented— One day, when it was time for a regular checkup, the medical operator opened the door to find a fine leporibeast standing by Snow Hunter's bed, huffing and kicking its front hooves. With great ceremony, she placed its reins into the medic's hands, saying it was a gift of gratitude for treating her condition. The medic, who was allergic to animal fur, began sneezing non-stop, but Snow Hunter mistook the tears in her eyes for tears of joy. The medical department spent three days deliberating what to do with this energetic leporibeast, and eventually resolved to ask Snow Hunter to return it to the wilderness when they found it trying to nibble at the medical equipment. Snow Hunter could not understand why and looked hurt that her gift was rejected: to her, that was the highest show of gratitude she could offer. After further dialogue, she learned that the common token of gratitude among the hunters would be good enough for this kind of situation: a bundle of meat jerky, savory and well-salted. This mountain delicacy was shared within the entire medical department to rave reviews. Perhaps there is still room for improvement in our Getting Started at Rhodes Island: Guidelines for New Operators.

Of all the legends of Kjerag, the 'mysterious creature of the mountains' is the one that Snow Hunter gets asked the most about. Legend has it that mysterious, beautiful creatures dwell on the mountains, appearing before those who lose their way in the storm, showing them the way home. It is said that many hunters owe their lives to these creatures, and Snow Hunter just happens to have a little white creature with her. According to her, however, it was she who saved the creature, Rift Cloudbeast, while out on a hunt, and shared her limited food with the weakened beastling for days.
Many operators were confused as to why she had to cut her own portion of food. Why not hunt more often? Was it because of the difficulties of hunting in a snowstorm? Snow Hunter's answer was that this was one of Kjeragandr's rules: Every being in the mountains, including the hunters, are part of Kjeragandr, sharing in Her soul in an eternal cycle of life. As such, they take only what they need. To take any more lives would be unnecessary killing. She could not do more hunting than necessary just for the Rift Cloudbeast, but she could also not stand idly by and watch it die, so she chose to share her own food with this being, who shared in Kjeragandr's blessing.
The Rift Cloudbeast seems completely oblivious to all of this, enjoying the comfort of Snow Hunter's quarters and occasionally playing with the Kjeragandr sculptures on the desk, which she hand-sculpted, a craft she has been studying since the day she started hunting on her own.
She steadfastly believes that Kjeragandr will protect her, her family, and everyone.

Many operators know of the three great clans of Kjerag, and the history of conflict between them. Snow Hunter comes from the Paleroche clan, while Pramanix, who introduced her to Rhodes Island, comes from the Silverash clan. The two of them seem to enjoy a good relationship with each other: Snow Hunter will sometimes ask Pramanix to braid her hair, while Pramanix often tells the story of how Snow Hunter saved her life and treated her wound. If not for her treatment, the wound on her right leg would likely force her to leave the harsh environment of Kjerag and live somewhere else. Besides, they can often be seen praying together as well.
Operators who see this might think that the feud between Clan Paleroche and Clan Silverash has been exaggerated, and that the younger generation is no longer concerned with their contentious past, but SilverAsh's presence is a reminder that not all is water under the bridge—
While operators going to visit Pramanix would normally pass by SilverAsh's room nearby, Snow Hunter prefers to go the long way around, avoiding going near his room.
She has told us that she does not know much about the history of the three clans. All she knows is that roaring trains have intruded into the quiet forests, and that the animals that used to live there were forced to flee their homes, leaving behind the carcasses of the ones that died of fright and hunger. It was against such a backdrop that she rescued the Rift Cloudbeast. She does not understand why people would pave concrete on Kjeragandr's body or dig a hole in it, causing a Catastrophe to befall them, which is how she lost her father.

It took a long time before Snow Hunter became comfortable talking about her father.
To her, her father was a great hunter, able to kill beasts several times his size with a single bolt and return safely from the mountains in a raging snowstorm. He was also a great craftsman who sculpted beautiful Kjeragandr sculptures with his callused fingers, supporting the family after her mother passed away. After she came down with Oripathy, it was her father who reassured her that he would find a way to cure her, that she would not need to worry about the future. But he himself died in the Catastrophe at the train station, and she found out through his effects that he had been acting as a spy to buy medicine for her.
She could not even find someone to blame. Did Kjeragandr punish her father for his betrayal? Was it her that made him betray his faith? Was she the one who was ultimately responsible for all this?
Snow Hunter found herself beset with anger and bewilderment. She had accompanied the Saintess on her Pilgrimage to find an answer from Kjeragandr, but she never knew what she was actually hoping for. Did she want Kjeragandr to show Herself in all Her glory to expel the outsiders who had drawn their swords? Did she want Kjeragandr to shower Her blessings on her arm and heal her Oripathy? Or did she want Kjeragandr to blow away the snowstorms, and let her quarry run docilely into her bolts? And after that, what then?
Snow Hunter vaguely realized that this was not what she wanted in her prayers to Kjeragandr, that this was not how blessings and divine punishments worked. She had no way to know what her father was thinking when his faith was shattered, and what internal struggle he might have had when he made the choice. But she remembered the solemn expression on his face when he inspected his sculptures, and the joy and love he showed every time he brought her medicine. At the end of the day, he was simply a father who wanted his child to live well, and he had already paid the price.
'Emotions are such complicated things. There are many things I still don't understand.' This was what Snow Hunter said to us in the end. What we do know is that she is firm and resolute as she faces the path ahead. Her past experience and the teachings of Kjeragandr will undoubtedly guide her path when she feels lost, helping her walk towards a brighter future one step at a time.

Kjeragandr on high, hear my prayer.
Let your blessings be upon my mother,
and my father,
and my brother and sister.
Let your blessings be upon those who have helped me, those who have cared for me, those who walk with me.
Bear witness, Kjeragandr on high, that my life will be my own, no matter what hardships await.

[Code Name] Hadiya
[Gender] Female
[Combat Experience] 3 Years
[Place of Birth] Columbia
[Date of Birth] Jul 22
[Race] Caprinae
[Height] 167cm
[Infection Status]
Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

[Physical Strength] Standard
[Mobility] Standard
[Physical Resilience] Excellent
[Tactical Acumen] Standard
[Combat Skill] Standard
[Originium Arts Assimilation] Normal

The Sargonian-Columbian Hadiya is a descendant of the Qarnsayf, a legendary warrior tribe of the desert. She joined Rhodes Island in Sargon as part of her ambition to improve her combat techniques. She currently receives training and participates in field missions at the Sargonian branch office of Rhodes Island.

Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Hadiya shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.19u/L
Before joining Rhodes Island, Operator Hadiya spent an extended time in the Sargonian wilderness without proper protection, resulting in BOCD numbers close to the infection threshold. As she is expected to spend significant time in the field, we have arranged additional tests in order to prepare proper protection for her. While Hadiya's awareness of the risks inherent in wilderness environments is lacking, she has proven cooperative with our work, which has greatly facilitated our efforts.

Based on her own account of her activities, she has been quite lucky to avoid contracting Oripathy so far. Unlike some tribal warriors, however, she is very receptive to scientific methods, and has already put in a request for other warriors from her tribe to receive similar checkups and training on Originium protection, pending approval by the Medical Department.
—Medical Department Note

Although Hadiya first encountered Rhodes Island in Sargon, and was assigned to the Sargonian branch after she was hired, it is obvious that she is not your average Sargonian.
Her style is very different from tribal warriors. She wields a staff with her right hand and a sword with her left, both containing complex mechanisms and axle-connected blades. The staff has foldable hooked blades on one end and a blunt hammer on the other, allowing her to employ both lethal and non-lethal means to neutralize enemies in close combat. Meanwhile, the short hilt of the sword makes it easy to perform thrusting motions when wielded on its own. An elaborate connector mechanism allows the two weapons to be combined into one, whereby the staff's hammer is retracted, the folding blades extended, and the shape of the sword's blade also changes, allowing her to respond to different situations and ranges. Hadiya had these weapons custom-made for her during her time in Columbia, and their design and construction clearly reflect Columbian technological thinking, making them very different from Sargonian weapons. The techniques she demonstrates in training are also different from traditional Sargonian techniques. She is an expert at utilizing cover and obstacles in close-quarters combat, relying on guile rather than strength, and creating an advantage through the versatility of her weapon. On the other hand, she is less comfortable fighting in wide-open spaces. She admits that she is still unfamiliar with the Sargonian wilderness, having developed her habits on the streets of Columbia and in training rooms. She recognizes that this is an area she needs to improve on as part of her new responsibilities, and she often approaches other Sargonian operators to pick their brains.

[Training Room Audio Log]
'Don't you find Hadiya's conversations with other Sargonian warriors really interesting?'
'What do you mean?'
'She always wants to learn the details of their weapons, how they're built, how they work, what environments they're good in.
'Most of the time, though, the only answer she gets is:
'Don't think. Just chop.'

The experience of growing up in Columbia will always be part of her. As she has often told other operators in the Sargon area, she knew that she was destined to come to this wilderness, but she also knows that it will hard to shake her Columbian habits, even once the glory of the Qarnsayf is restored.

'I grew up in a small community in a nomadic city,' said Hadiya while chatting with other operators during break time. 'It wasn't a very wealthy district, but it was always lively, with people coming from all kinds of places, and Sargon is just one of them.
'Every group has its own unique customs, character, and views. To me, though, it always felt so cohesive.
'Everyone's habits and pastimes had become Columbianized. Watching Wrankwood movies over soda and fried fowlbeast, making a fuss during district elections, and so on.
'The movies were great though! I should bring the latest pop music next time.'

While Hadiya is happy to talk about the culture and customs of Columbia, she has never shown an intention to import them to Sargon. When asked about the reason, she said she did not want to do so, because it would ruin the purity of Sargon in her mind.
In her veneration of the wilderness, she is, indeed, a proper Sargonian—a remark from many of her colleagues.

Hadiya went through many hardships when rebuilding her tribe.
The name Qarnsayf exists only in historical records. Their territory no longer exists, nor have they left behind any extant relics, or first-hand witnesses to their exploits. This is why many lords ameer privately harbor doubts about the veracity of the legendary tribe's existence, even though The Book of Sargon contains detailed records of the Qarnsayf and their battles.
Hadiya's father's generation claimed to be the descendants of the Qarnsayf, and passed down their ancestors' teachings and the responsibility of rebuilding the tribe to hers. Although their appearance matches the depictions of the Qarnsayf in the records, and it is true that many Qarnsayf tribesmen left Sargon to become mercenaries, this is hardly enough to convince the Padishah to grant them new territory, much less make their name known throughout the tribes.
The local Padishah's challenge presented even more obstacles to her path. In order to earn the Padishah's trust and have him officially recognize the tribe and its territory, Hadiya must earn the recommendation of fifteen lords ameer and obtain their tokens—no mean feat when each one has a different demand. Defeating a lord ameer's guards in combat is merely the first step: some would not even give her the opportunity until she passed a test of history, which is hardly her strong suit. As such, at this time, Hadiya has only earned the approval of two lords ameer who allowed her to challenge their soldiers directly, and there is a long way to go until she completes the Padishah's task.
Hadiya has never complained about this. She is often seen in the break room watching Columbian movies, or chatting with colleagues about city life, showing no sign of worry about the progress of the challenge.
When others ask about it, her answer is this: If you fail, try again until you succeed.
She has never doubted that she will succeed.

[Columbian Department of Immigration Audio Log 044]
'Here are the reports on the ten Sargonians. Well, nine Sargonians now.'
'What happened?'
'One was deathly ill before crossing the border. Already dead by the time the troops found them.'
'Where are they? Still in custody?'
'Yes. It's a band of wandering mercenaries, not immigrants who entered through official channels. The military has concerns about their background and doesn't want to let them in.'
'Why don't they just deport them? Why hand them over to us?'
'Deport them where? Their employer, well, doesn't exist anymore, so that's out of the question. And the situation in Sargon is pretty chaotic right now. These ten seem to be from the same tribe, and most likely from somewhere our intel indicates a massacre occurred. The military is concerned that they might resort to desperate measures if not handled properly. I was there at the detention center, and I saw the kind of look in their eyes you only see in people who've seen hell. I'd only seen it in veterans of the Revolutionary War before.'
'So General Sfax doesn't want to be responsible for whatever happens if they're let loose. They want us to make the decision.'
'Do you want to review the report?'
'No need. Tell the general to let them in. Our mission is to absorb different types of immigrants from various places, and these Sargonians fit our needs.'
'Yes, sir, I'll let him know.'
'One more thing. Mark their papers and file them under 'Special Immigrants.' For reference when drafting future management policies.'
'Yes, sir.'

She could hardly feel her legs anymore.
Through the swaying light of the firepot, she looked at the lord ameer sitting behind the table, who was gazing at her with narrowed eyes. She knew she had to maintain control of her body and not waver, because the slightest sign of weakness would give him an excuse to deny her hard work.
First, the trial of recitement. She used the techniques that Anat taught her.
Second, the trial of stamina. Long years of training carried her through.
At last, the duel with the lord ameer's elite guard. There was no time for rest before this last trial. Thoroughly exhausted, she faced off against the hulking shieldguard. None of the faces illuminated by firelight were cheering for her. She could hear the crowd roar whenever the guard parried her attacks—
'Finish her off!'
When she hooked the edge of the shield with her staff and leapt into the air with the momentum of her opponent's charge, then flicked the sword to unfold the blades and cut the guard's necklace, none of the sounds around the stage mattered anymore.
'As per our agreement, victory is mine, lord ameer.' She could feel the words in her throat, but was not sure if she actually vocalized them or not.
The reaction of the lord ameer told her that she had. It was only her third victory, with twelve more to go, but she knew she was on the right path.
She took the token and turned around to walk towards the exit. Her legs had been numb, but now they were strong again, and her steps were no longer heavy.
She left behind the light of the firepots, and gazed out at the wilderness to see the sun rising upon the horizon.

[Code Name] Akkord
[Gender] Female
[Combat Experience] None
[Place of Birth] Leithanien
[Date of Birth] Aug 11
[Race] Caprinae
[Height] 165cm
[Infection Status]
Confirmed Infected by medical examination.

[Physical Strength] Normal
[Mobility] Normal
[Physical Resilience] Normal
[Tactical Acumen] Normal
[Combat Skill] Normal
[Originium Arts Assimilation] Standard

Akkord, real name Tonia Klang, is a tuner hailing from a remote Leithanian town. She was referred to Rhodes Island for treatment after contracting Oripathy in a soundfield core overload accident caused by a snowstorm. She currently helps out with Rhodes Island's music scene, while assisting in battle as a caster.

Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3%
Small traces of infection are visible on the surface of the body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.22u/L
Akkord contracted Oripathy early, and comes into contact with Originium components regularly in her work, but she observes proper protection and is diligent about receiving treatment. Her condition is currently stable with no sign of infection spreading.

Operator Akkord has a habit of 'listening' in her daily work and inspections. She explains it as capturing the specific frequencies of the target's soundfield, and adding 'tags' to them in her notes.
The relationship between this behavior and her tuning work is unclear, but maintenance logs across different cities show a pattern: When Akkord notices any changes in the subject's tags, she will instantly check the audio facilities in the subject's block, make necessary adjustments, or perform extra inspections around the area.
The Medical Department is reserving judgment on the uniqueness of her hearing. Assessors believe it is not absolute pitch in the traditional sense of the word, but an identification method based on perception and experience.
It must be noted that Akkord has never publicly discussed the specific relationship between her tags and the tagged subjects, and her notes contain no decipherable information.
On the whole, we do not believe there are significant risks associated with this habit at this time, though continued observation is recommended regarding why and how she uses this ability in special missions.

The town's train station was always noisy at dusk. Miners chatting and laughing as they return from work, children chasing each other over the tracks, and the fires of smelters roaring in the distance. Tonia slowly pushed her old soundfield tuner through the crowd. It was a heavy machine with creaking gears that sounded like they could fall apart at any moment. She was headed towards the broadcasting speakers at the town square, which had become distorted by age and sounded like they had been put through sand and rubble.
The people in town were not particularly hostile to her, nor were they particularly friendly. She was one of those people who don't do 'real work'. To the townsfolk, a little bit of Arts was all that was needed if some facility in town broke down, and they were not entirely wrong. As such, they did not bother to ask Tonia for help most of the time.
'Doesn't seem like her Arts got any better, even after she got infected.'
'I heard her grades were pretty ordinary. Didn't inherit her father's musical talent, I guess.'
'Then what's the point of getting infected—'
'Shh, don't say that...'
Tonia pretended not to hear these comments around town. She simply inserted her tuner's pin into the speakers, and turned the knob to minimize the noise while listening. Slowly but steadily, she tuned the sound of wind, furnaces, and footsteps into the waveform, until the screechiness was gone, and the broadcast sounded nice and smooth again.
Only a few nearby miners seemed to notice that the ambient sounds had become more pleasant. They nodded but said nothing to Tonia, as if they were simply acknowledging something that was always supposed to happen. Tonia put away the machine and pushed it away. She knew she was neither a scholar nor a smith, and she would not leave any signature or adage on her work, like the ones on the plaques hung up in the town hall. Even in such a remote town, in the most ordinary workshop, the people only spoke of the strongest and most worthy to be remembered. However, Tonia heard the weak and strong sounds just the same. Even the tiniest tremolo could not escape her.
Tonia felt herself stripped from familiar society and systems, layer by layer—on the results board at school, in the soundfield accident that snowy night... Sometimes she felt she had gotten used to the things that happened to her. What other choice was there? But she was happy, for the soundfield in the square was now in harmony, and she saw a few fowlbeasts perch on the station's window sill, a sight she had not seen for a while.
'How to get the musical Arts on the murals to resonate better with the cries of fowlbeasts... I should come back tomorrow and re-tune it.'
Tonia thought as she pushed the tuner on the way back.

'Is this... music theory? Or some kind of performance instruction?'
At the operator's question, Akkord realized she had dropped her old notebook. The operator who picked it up was reading through it with admiration in her eyes. The cover of the notebook was so worn that it had become glossy, while the edges of the pages had curled up from frequent turning. Akkord felt a tinge of embarrassment, unsure whether to take the notebook back, or answer the question.
'The wind swirling in the notches of the stone spires creates sounds that do not belong to the original tune. If they are not eliminated, they could spread through the town along the cracks of the spire.'
'Music flowing through the seams of copper tubes may become sharpened due to contraction in the cold. Mixing in wooden harmonies will make it less piercing.'
'In rainy season, the rhythms caused by water dripping at the old clock tower may distort the soundfield, requiring regular maintenance, or passages with a different texture to counterbalance it...'
Only a few wall lights remained on in the archives, casting their light on the paper. The operator read through the notebook carefully with curiosity: There was nothing like music theory or intricate formulae, but only casually written tips and guidelines, combining Arts knowledge and everyday experience.
'Just some informal adjustment tricks. Nothing significant,' answered Akkord.
'But these are really useful! They would be great teaching materials. Not that I know much about music, but I know you always use musical Arts in the right situations, without any clashing melodies...'
Teaching materials? Akkord was not listening to the latter half of what the operator was saying. She was thinking that such teaching materials were unneeded in Leithanien, as there were no special Arts in the notes, nor would they be considered musical creations. On this ship, however, someone was reading them quietly under the lights, even treating them as genuine knowledge.
Akkord recalled the nights in Zwillingstürme, how the nameless tuners restored the harmony of the city's soundfield. Now, on this behemoth far away from home, she realized that these experiences, which she thought nobody cared about, could at least make other tuners feel less lonely.
'Can I try tuning the musical equipment in my room by following your notes?'
The sound coming from beside her pulled Akkord back from the city's music to the Rhodes Island archive room. She smiled bashfully and nodded. Perhaps, these experiences she thought nobody cared about would spread even beyond the tuners.

[Audio Log]
'...On the count of three, we'll start singing together.'
'One, two, three—'
'......'
'Goodness, who just went up into the atmosphere?'
'It wasn't me... Wait, maybe it was? Sorry, I always seem to lose the key when I'm nervous.'
'Heh, I wish I brought earplugs!'
'Stop laughing, you sang even worse than I did! You dragged me off-key!'
'Alright, alright. None of you were especially in harmony just now.'
'Yeah, I know we're tone-deaf, Akkord...'
'I was talking about the hesitation in your voices. Try think it this way: When you're out of tune, you're just in different positions. Some go up, some go down, some go here, some go there. And that's what gives a song its range, right?'
'The audience must see us as a flock of squawking fowlbeasts.'
'Fowlbeasts seem so in harmony when they're together, don't they? I don't think they discuss how to sing beforehand, or care about how others want them to sing. They just sing the way they want.'
'Is it really the same thing?'
'Of course.'
'......'
'How do you want us to sing, then, Akkord? We're performing in front of the whole ship in one hour.'
'Sing what you can. It's my job to get these different voices in different positions together in the same place without stepping on each other's toes.'
'Isn't that... cheating?'
'No, I'm simply reigning in stray sounds and getting them to walk together. You have a bright soprano, but you're too scared to let it come out. You, you have a solid bass like a rock. No need to be scared, I'll catch it. As for you, you have a beautiful tone, and you're the one who put your heart and soul into these lyrics. All you need to do is sing what you want to express.'
'Are you really talking about us, Akkord? You make it sound as though... all of us could be useful.'
'Not just useful. Indispensable. You all enjoyed the process of writing the song, didn't you? You stand here now because you love it. All you need to do is sing what you love. Besides, Maestro Czerny wrote this song for you to sing together.'
'What if it still sounds bad?'
'All the more reason to sing out loud, so that no one can ignore how bad it sounds. Of course, I'll probably have to go with you to beg for permission to hold another event...'
'Haha... alright, let's try again?'
'Let's try again. All you need to do is open your mouths. Leave the rest to me.'

Tonia rarely participated in her class's creative showcases while at school. Her notebooks were filled with strange symbols, arrows, and overlapping waveforms, but rarely complete melodies. Her classmates used instruments or song to create musical Arts, but she preferred a little audio recorder, carrying it through streets, markets, and old workshops, collecting those authentic sounds around her—the knocking of hammer on metal, the low humming of winds gliding past the eaves on a snowy night, or the screeching sound of trains braking as sparks fly. She broke the sounds down into fundamental vibrations, and attempted to recreate their texture and temperature with Arts. To most of her peers and teachers, it was an act of documentation, not creation, a mosaic lacking in soul. Tonia never argued. All she did was put away her device and walk down from the stage after each showcase with her head bowed, through scattered applause and silent skepticism from the crowd.
Years later, Tonia was in the Rhodes Island workshop, testing a piece of audio equipment. She knocked it lightly with a tuning fork, listening to the echoes bounce inside the casing. The monitor next to it flashed; the curved line on the screen fluctuated. In a split second, it looked just like the waves she wrote in her notebook in her youth.
Tonia gazed upon the curved line. Her fingertip stayed on the knob, as though trying to capture a familiar feeling—neither melody nor rhythm, but a position that gave her certainty that the sound belonged to her. The equipment hummed, and she bowed her head again to record the sound in her recorder. Tonia was not sure what she could eventually do with the collected sounds, but was in no hurry to answer the question.

[Code Name] Nasti
[Gender] Female
[Combat Experience] 15 Years
[Place of Birth] Kazdel
[Date of Birth] Apr 9
[Race] Sarkaz
[Height] 171cm
[Infection Status]
Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.

[Physical Strength] Excellent
[Mobility] Excellent
[Physical Resilience] Standard
[Tactical Acumen] Standard
[Combat Skill] Outstanding
[Originium Arts Assimilation] Standard

Nasti Lunorey, director of Rhine Lab's Engineering Section and one of Columbia's foremost authorities in engineering, as well as an expert in applied linguistics. With a reference from Saria, she has entered into a long-term memorandum of cooperation with Rhodes Island and provides support for various projects as a special consultant to the Engineering Department.

Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be non-infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Nasti shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.13u/L
Operator Nasti lived in Kazdel for five years during her childhood and spent more than a decade traveling across Terra. That she has been able to avoid infection is a combination of good luck and extreme care taken with protective measures.

'My goals require a healthy body, that's all.'
—Nasti

'But your calluses are too thick!'
—A passing Elf

Nasti accepted our offer to act as a special engineering consultant soon after we established contact through Saria.
According to the operator from the Trimounts branch who brought the contract to Nasti, Rhine Lab did not prepare any ceremony or even an office room for the signing of this important agreement. A haughty Forte researcher by the name of Sky Jagger led him to an underground facility, pointed at a door, and said, 'The director is inside' before leaving. The operator opened the door, his head filled with question marks, and was met with a shocking sight: hundreds of giant ants wearing yellow safety helmets barreling around the room, charging at him the moment they saw him. He dropped the contract, which was immediately stampeded into pieces. Then Nasti emerged from amongst the ants and approached him, saying, 'Sorry, I had inspection work I couldn't get away from.'
Having gotten over the fright of Rhine Lab apparently turning on Rhodes Island, the operator noticed that the giant ants were in fact branch-shaped robots, sharing the same origin as the device on Nasti's belt. A masterpiece by Rhine's Director of Engineering, these incantation-driven creations were inspecting the energy supply system using their dexterous branches to complete various delicate tasks, while the safety helmets protected their cores.
With the contract badly damaged, the operator apologized to Nasti and offered to reschedule the signing, only to be surprised again by the reaction of the impassive director. Nasti took a section of a paper tape floating around her and had the operator dictate the general outline of the contract. As he spoke, words appeared on the tape, then a robot stepped on his foot, gave him a pen, gesturing for him to sign it.
The operator would later describe the scene in vivid detail to others whenever he had the opportunity: complex pipelines arranged like a witchcraft array in a strange underground space, signing one end of an incantation-woven paper tape as the aloof Banshee signed the other, while hundreds of giant ants wearing safety helmets hustled around them. For a moment, he thought he had entered the territory of some mysterious Sami tribe. It seems there is still much on Terra that he does not know about.

'An incantation is a Banshee's promise. It will never fade, as long as I exist.'

When speaking of the 'Rhine Lab Ten', Nasti is seldom the first name to come to mind. Kristen is an icon unto her own. Muelsyse has as many friends as she has water clones. Ferdinand is so strict he can scare a crying intern into shutting up with a single look. Maryam's exploits have won him many fans in Columbia's extreme adventuring community. Meanwhile, there is little to even say about the Director of Engineering, who spends her time moving from construction site to construction site, rarely showing her face in public. Even in her rare appearances, she hardly talks or shows any expression on her face.
That is, until a junior researcher from the Ecological Section repeatedly came across Muelsyse, the director of the Ecological Section, watching the same home renovation show with great interest. Among the many interests of Muelsyse, from games to fashion to photography, home renovation was not known to be one of them. The Rhine Lab gossip mill quickly ramped up and soon discovered the truth: Muelsyse had her eyes on a special guest who participated anonymously across multiple seasons, fascinating the audience with bold, avant-garde designs that emphasize unconventional spatial order. In a season themed around future living, the designer built a home based on the concept of musbeast wheels, with seven living spaces in different styles rotating on a wheel, maximizing both usage and fun. Muelsyse made a compilation of episodes featuring that designer and sent it to the designer herself: Nasti.
This discovery soon became the talk of Rhine Lab from the corridors to the break rooms. Everyone had a hard time connecting that paragon of avant-garde architecture on the show to the reserved, pragmatic, and meticulous head of Engineering. Later, it was revealed that it was Jara, head of HR, who initially arranged for Nasti to join the show to 'maintain activity'. Contracts for subsequent seasons, however, were signed by Nasti of her own accord.

'Unlike the research sections, Engineering has a limited budget for creative experimentation. I saw no reason to turn down an offer to pay me to build weird houses.'
This was Nasti's answer when someone mustered the courage to ask her.

[Audio log of a lecture to new employees by Nasti, Director of Engineering for Rhine Lab]
'Engineering is Rhine Lab's busiest section. We have to coordinate with the other operational sections, while also providing engineering support for Structural, Ecological, Energy, Originium Art, and Scientific Investigation Section, in an endless journey to fulfill their demands. This is my advice: don't think of yourself as the scientists' friend. Read every word on those proposals and blueprints carefully, and tell them which are a matter of laying the bricks and tightening the screws, and which are pipe dreams they need to wake up from.
'Energy's facility proposals are generally properly validated. Ferdinand may be an arrogant asshole, but he knows what he's doing.'
......
'Be on your guard when dealing with Ecological. Don't let Muelsyse find your weakness.
'Defense... Saria's former department. A bunch of tough customers to deal with. In its role in assuring the safety of Rhine Lab's projects, the Defense Section has more concerns to consider, and its methods are more resolute. Saria is the new Control now, but their style has not changed. Saria herself has a serious case of OCD. I was in charge of renovating her office, and it was a long, arduous process.
'Power supplies and emergency equipment for Originium Art must be built to the highest standard. As for Dorothy, I am very familiar with people like her. They have too many people to worry about, too many things they want to do, and too many things to lose, but they deserve respect.'
......
'May I ask a question, Director Nasti?'
'Go on.'
'When you described the other directors, it sounded like they are more than just co-workers to you...'

[Industry Commentary: Braving the Forbidden—Reform or Rehash?]
There seems to be little point in talking about 'forbidden' areas in a land that is 90% uninhabited.
On this land tilled by Catastrophe for thousands of years, even wilderness level enough for nomadic cities to traverse is rare, much less fertile soil suited for farming. For city-dwellers who think fowlbeast meat is grown in supermarkets directly in their packages, ready to be cooked, the nomadic cities and the wilderness visible from their routes are the entirety of Terra. They do not think of other places as 'distant' or 'dangerous', because they do not think of those places at all.
As such, 'travel' in the traditional sense is more like a vacation. Caravan International Travel Agency can take you to Sami, but all you will see is a well-furnished Sami-style resort village. It will feel no different from a Columbian nomadic city, at least once you spend a few days acclimating to the cold.
In recent years, however, Columbian tourism has become fascinated with the forbidden. News reports of the wealthy hiring guides to take them into forbidden areas are a regular occurrence, and travel agencies have started marketing these 'forbidden tours'. Naturally, the authorities responded by stepping up their control of such areas. Last year, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, the Columbian Park Police, and the army's Mobile Cavalry came to an accord regarding management division of the Bleached Wasteland, drafting a patrol route that fully covers the region.
As for the reason...

'It's true that enforcement has gotten stricter, but that has nothing to do with those so-called 'forbidden tours'. Two tour guides dressed up in military uniforms pretend to check your papers, then you take a few photos in a place that looks empty enough—that's all that 'forbidden tour' crap is about.
'If you want to see caverns with naturally occurring liquefied Originium, or Feranmut carcasses lying in the desert—the stuff you'd have to risk your hide to see...
'Then look for Ferne Barn.
'Me? Forget it, I'm not taking anyone with me, no way.
'Ferne's the only one with the skills AND the willingness to bring people along. You wanna go, find her.'
—Operator Asbestos, when asked about 'forbidden tours'

None of the children came to Dad's funeral, but there was an uninvited guest who interrupted the ritual with blaring sirens. A potbellied cop poked his head out of the patrol car, saying he had received complaints from parents about someone by the name of Martin Barn, who deceived children with tales of gold-scaled sandbeasts and the like—
The cop stopped mid-sentence, took a look at us, then at the name on the coffin, and left without another word.
Sheriff Jones of Trenton—I nailed the name to the wall when I founded the travel agency, hoping to prove to him one day that Dad wasn't a scammer, and gold-scaled sandbeasts were real.
In the last few years, I proved a lot of things to a lot of people. Some didn't believe there were nomadic cities outside of Columbia, some believed the Pioneers' treasure was hidden in the Bleached Wasteland... I let them see the truth with their own eyes, but was never able to prove the existence of gold-scaled sandbeasts.
I had theories. The steppe-dwelling sandbeasts usually have multiple layers of backfins in order to blend into their surroundings, which could easily be mistaken for scales at a distance. Maybe sandbeasts that dwell in golden steppes rich in Originium really do look like they have golden scales. Another theory was that the people of Rim Billiton had tamed small sandbeasts for use in the mines—the capillaries in their backfins can help with determining air conditions in the tunnels, and people sometimes would paste golden foil on their backfins for easier identification. Was that what Dad saw?
It makes sense, doesn't it? But there's no proof. It helps people understand how these stories could come about, but it doesn't stop them from thinking Dad was lying.
Besides, Sheriff Jones passed away two years ago.
—Ferne Barn, on a rare occasion when she spoke about her father

Operator Titi almost immediately became integrated into the Rhodes Island community.
Her adventure began as soon as she parted ways with the HR operator who showed her the main facilities. There was hardly a corner of Rhodes Island that she didn't explore. After dining at the cafeteria, she exchanged a rare photocopy of an old Vine-Bead Court cookbook for Operator Matterhorn's collection of Kjeragi recipes. While visiting the Engineering Department, she expertly repaired an important part using glue meant for relic restoration. She even wandered into the mobility layer, making friends with the Sarkaz boiler workers on her first day.
As we got to know her, however, we grew even more perplexed. The seemingly insignificant accessories she wears are in fact valuable ancient relics, which she seems to treat with complete nonchalance. Her white ribbon in particular is more than decorative: driven by Originium Arts, it practically serves as an extra arm, allowing her to grab distant objects, and move or support herself during activities such as climbing. It is also a medium for her to take notes, record her discoveries and data, or even act as a cheat sheet for public speaking.
We soon learned that, while making friends with Titi is easy, truly getting to know her is a different story.

[Weapon Evaluation]
Titi's staff stands in contrast to her short stature. At her checkup, we immediately found that the staff amplified her Arts considerably. The antiques she wears and the classical design of the staff gave us the impression that it was a family heirloom passed down through generations, but she had in fact designed and assembled it herself.
Titi says that its design was inspired by ancient Sargonian artifacts. The scarab sealed inside a piece of golden amber in the middle represents eternal life and resurrection, an ancient symbol dating back to Lugalszargus, the 'Shah of Past and Future,' making it an ideal fit for her conservation Arts. Our discussion turned into an impromptu semiotics lecture, as at one point we thought the symbol represented some kind of power boost Arts, a misconception that she soon dispelled.
'Power boost? Oh, that's because of the seven amplifiers I installed on the staff, on the ring around the amber.'

[A Trimounts University Transcript] Museum Design: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates a thorough understanding of modern museology theory, as well as a mind open enough to effectively implement new media to enrich the exhibition experience. Can sometimes be overly fixated on new forms, in particular conceptual interaction designs advocated by the Columbia Art and Design Center, leading to the exhibition's content being overshadowed by the presentation. Archaeological Analysis and Technology: A- (Joint course with Trimounts Academy of Technology) Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates high proficiency in technological methods for analyzing the materials and techniques of relics. Occasionally prone to spur-of-the-moment ideas, resulting in outlandish experiments, and insists on analyzing the failed results. Conservation and Restoration: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates excellent grasp of conservation and restoration techniques for relics of various materials. Capable of independently coming up with restoration proposals for working with heavily damaged artifacts, plans that are often risky, but the results have generally exceeded expectations. The only issue being occasional violations of lab rules and protocols—do not use the lab's specially blended glue to stick your classmate's shoe soles back on! ... The transcript is a long one, with far more credits on it than needed to graduate. It includes her compulsory coursework, subjects tangentially connected to her major like international history, languages, art history, architecture, and folklore, but also courses like 'Ingredient Analysis of Sami Herbal Remedies', 'Principles of Automated Flying Machine Control', and 'Literary Analysis of Flowers of Quinde and Kerespereia', taken for reasons unknown. Even more surprising is that she got an 'A-' in most of her coursework and excelled academically by any definition, yet had very few full marks in any of her courses: the instructors usually docked her points here and there for unusual reasons. Titi did not seem especially concerned with her grades—what mattered more to her was whether the course was interesting, and her definition of an interesting course was very different from others. While most look for variety, lively pacing, and humor, she judges courses by whether they satisfy her curiosity and stimulate her desire to explore further. 'I went to Columbia because I thought it would be fun. I had just graduated from school in Menat-Ha'mait when a Columbian merchant showed up with a bunch of newfangled things and told me that Trimounts University accepted students from all over Terra. It made me want to check it out for myself. I didn't think much about the distance from Menat-Ha'mait to Trimounts, or how I was actually going to get accepted and enroll. I just thought I would cross that bridge when I got there.'

Operator Titi describes her younger self as a 'free range wild child'. Her father was known as a ne'er-do-well amongst Menat-Ha'mait's nobility, having no interest in fame or fortune, only literature, and in particular in collecting books brought back to Sargon from occupied Minos. Never in great health, he fell ill when Titi was young and virtually stopped leaving the house altogether. To Titi, her father was like a plant that grew on the chair of his study. He would tell her stories if she went to find him, and if she did not, he did not concern himself with what she was doing. As such, she enjoyed more freedom than most noble children. She had plenty of room to explore, think, and imagine, and to reveal the laws and truth behind what she saw, what she was interested in. Her conclusions were not necessarily correct, and her ideas young and naive, but she had arrived at them on her own. The process of thinking helped her build trust in her own judgment, taught her how to obtain the information she wanted, and opened doors to new horizons. It took a long time for her to understand that there were many things that did not need to be said. How to explore, how to study, how to defuse hostility, how to help friends, how to find one's path forward, how to commit to what one thinks should be done... she had already learned all these things from the stories her father told her, and her mother's tacit approval and indulgence. [Book Excerpt] ...And so the silent Siopi returned to his homeland, but still he never spoke. 'You are friendly and outgoing. You never know if you might accidentally reveal the secret you are trying to keep in conversation.' The safest way, therefore, was to never speak. Once full of vigor and spirit when he left home, the young man now shut himself away, shunned contact with others, and died as silently as he lived. It was only a long time later, when the news of victory came from afar, that his fellows learned the secret he carried, and thus he became known as Siopi, the Silent Hero. —Excerpt from Vol.3 of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, 1101, Varjavandabad Museum Press [Book Review] Scholars are excited about the publication of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, and for good reason. Mr. Khnum Nasutu Mashayer has long been known for his extensive collection of Minoan literature, and this six-volume collection, totaling more than three thousand pages, is more than just a compilation of the famous legends collected in the Mashayer Archives and their many variations, but also of rare oral traditions that he personally collected during his time in Minos. It is a landmark in scholarship that will undoubtedly be cited by researchers for decades to come. It is perhaps also worth noting that the publication of this work was sponsored by Mr. Mashayer's widow, and it was compiled and edited by their daughter. This is itself something of a legend.

We initially thought that the entity known as 'Mio' who accompanies Operator Titi was simply an ordinary Feline Beast Steward, although in hindsight there were certainly telling signs. Mio is very similar to Titi in its sociability, and its investigation of Rhodes Island took place concurrently with Titi's explorations. Mio quickly found its turf, claiming the best fresh fin belly from the cafeteria every morning, as well as a cushion on the sunniest spot on the bridge, though it does not visit every day.
Other operators claim to occasionally see a small, strange-looking Feline who often accompanies Titi, at times getting her out of tight spots, while at others getting into arguments with her, like two close yet bickering friends.
This has led to us theorizing about Mio's true nature... by now, we have grown rather familiar with such beings. For now, at least, there seems to be little cause for concern, since Mio's intervention has been limited to providing occasional assistance to Titi and filling its own stomach.

[Classified Log]
Hey, I picked the girl myself, I can't very well let her fend for herself. I like her personality, and she's not burdened by stuff like legacy or history, like so many other humans. Getting out of the Grand Bazaar wasn't easy, and I'd like nothing more than to have some real free time with nothing to worry about, but I guess the girl's not gonna stay put.
She and that damn curiosity of hers. Yeah, I know where she wants to go, but the depths of the desert is just not a nice place. The old Shah... yes, interesting fellow. Woof and I liked him, but his one-time dream, his discoveries in the south, his invincible army, and all his outlandish ideas, have all been twisted beyond recognition. As for the current Shahanshah, the lion who has lain low in the depths of the desert for many years... Has his silence and inaction been by choice, or has something happened to that ancient city in the sands, something beyond the control of puny humans? I don't know, and I don't particularly care to know. Frankly, I would prefer not to return to Shar-Agade, if I had a choice.
You're an interesting one too, Doctor... There are many of my kind here. I know they are uneasy too. It's a fresh, unfamiliar feeling, and I don't like it one bit.

Operator Titi's time in Minos clearly left a deep impression on her, but when we asked for her thoughts on the trip, her answer was not what we expected.
'For a long time I've been thinking about a question, one that my mother and teachers have asked me as well: where will my curiosity take me?
'The incident at the museum planted the seed of an idea in my mind, and the journey to Minos made it sprout. My curiosity about history, society and how it works, science and how it develops ultimately comes from a desire to learn the reasons behind things, the things that shape us and our society, and make us who we are today.
'Having visited Athenius, I now know that stories of heroes form the roots of Minos, the desires of all Minoans converging upon the concept of 'hero'. What about us? What are the roots of Sargon, and what is our common goal, our shared aspiration? I'm afraid I don't know the answer, yet.
'But I think I'll find the answer one day, when I've gained sufficient knowledge. Or when the day comes that I visit the ancient city with over a thousand years of history.'

A caladium plant on one of the Convalescent Garden's shelves was the first to notice that something was off with Lena. Highly sensitive to changes in moisture, the plant had heretofore received the most tender care possible in the greenhouse, but now the edges of the leaves had begun to grow yellow, only returning to their previous color when Podenco discovered the issue and recalibrated the humidifier. Numerous minor incidents like this continued to occur throughout the week—pruning shears not being returned to their proper place, pesticide cans being filled with water, plant names spelled wrong on fragrance tags... When Podenco witnessed the normally steady and dependable Lena mix up pepper and cardamom, resulting in a sneezing fit, she was convinced of one thing: her performance evaluation had begun.
Lena had always been meticulous about the Convalescent Garden, after all. She hardly ever made errors, and would certainly not break the rules that she herself had set. She had built the garden from a few seeds and design books that she brought from her homeland, carefully picking the right flowers to grow, and developing it into a space for fragrance therapy. It was a labor of love, her pride, and one of the most popular hangouts for Rhodes Island operators.
It thus came as a shock when Podenco anxiously completed her seventeenth 'evaluation item', and learned that Lena was leaving to become the supervisor of the Athenius office. Perhaps this trip home had special meaning to Lena, or perhaps she received a letter from an old acquaintance inviting her to reveal some hidden past... The empathetic Perro sniffled as she expressed her worries to an HR operator while preparing a parting gift for Lena.

Why am I going back to Minos? Heh, tell Podenco not to overthink it. I knew Rhodes Island was going to establish a new office in Athenius, and it just made perfect sense that I should be involved. I was a little concerned about what would happen to the garden, but she has been particularly passionate about her work lately. It would have been a much harder decision if not for her. Huh? A performance evaluation? Oh dear, I didn't even realize I've been causing so much trouble for her... I suppose the prospect of returning home has made me nervous.
—Lena's explanation when submitting her disembarkment application

Many came to see the scion of the famous Athopoulou family when the Rhodes Island office was first established. From her botanical fragrance, to her gentle words, to the meticulous craftsmanship of her dress... everything about her was the very image of a well-bred young lady. She took young patients into the hills to pick herbs on sunny days, teaching them about the leaves and roots of medicinal plants, and the process that turned them into medicine to relieve pain. She told children who feared that their illness would prevent them from becoming heroes that they themselves would be the first person they saved, and it would be their first step on the path to becoming a hero.
Surprisingly, Dr. Lena has received mixed reviews in the office's recent patient surveys. One patient complained that she had banned her from drinking, catching her in under thirty minutes no matter which establishment she went to and preventing her from emulating Bacchus the Drunken Hero. Another lamented that he could not do the work he loved anymore, as he was no longer allowed to swing a hammer with his Originium-covered arm to make weapons in the traditional manner.
Most patients did not believe that the gentle doctor would use forceful measures, until one day a hulking and ferocious patient came rushing out of the consultation room to complain about her at the front desk. The man, a well-known ruffian, claimed that she had insulted his veneration of Heraces, and was trying to record his name in a book so that everyone would know he was a weak Infected. But he quickly lowered his raised fist at the sight of her coming out of the consultation room with her staff in hand, calmly explaining that registration was necessary for the establishment of an emergency medical system, and that the man's actions had demonstrated that he does not truly venerate the heroes, only the muscles that allowed him to bully the weak. She prescribed medicine for the troublemaker, and a bottle of pheromones labeled 'Your Heroic Spirit'.
The concept of 'hero' is a vague one, and everyone's understanding of 'heroic spirit' is different. The idea that Oripathy saps the heroic spirit, an ancient saying of unknown origin, has become a widespread belief in Minos. Even without discrimination from others, those suffering from Oripathy will leave the temples of their own accord, abandon their dreams, and even turn to a life of crime. Fortunately, operators at the office know that all they need to do with patients who have given in to despair is drag them into Lena's consultation room, and their dependable supervisor will use the fragrances of plants to calm her countrymen down.

The HR operator lost his way when he came to the 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden' for the first time. When he asked two Athenians where to find the supervisor of the local office, one said that the 'Flora of Athopoulou' was the only Oripathy doctor he knew, before being interrupted by his companion, who said, 'Do not compare an Infected to a hero, even if Dr. Lena has indeed done a lot for us.'
Flora is one of the heroes worshipped by Minoans, the legendary gardener of the 'Mountain-Rimmed Garden'. It is said that she had a superhuman affinity for plants, being instinctively in tune with the breath of nature, even bringing back dead flowers to life. She is the patron hero of Minoans who worked with plants, herbs, and perfumes, and Operator Perfumer's family was no exception. The Athopoulous were once one of the most famous families of Athenius, one that both gardeners and fashion-seeking merchants depended on. The family has long since fallen from its high perch, and most of its members have left Athenius, but there are many who still remember the former head of the family, Steros Athopoulou, and his daughter who left for distant lands at a young age.
Having learned of this past, the HR operator now sat in Perfumer's consultation room, listening to grateful patients call her the 'Flora of Athopoulou'. Seeing no reaction from Lena, the curious operator asked if she felt uncomfortable with the title. She looked surprised for a moment, then answered in the negative.
Returning to the office months later, the operator found that patients were no longer calling Lena by that lengthy title. A short distance away, a smartly dressed, gray-haired Vulpo with a cold expression on her face was writing up a citizen who had committed an offense. She stopped the operator when she saw the Rhodes Island's logo on his clothes, and their conversation was recorded as follows:
'How much do you know about Lena—or rather, 'Operator Perfumer'? How much do you know about the Athopoulou family?
'You've heard what the patients called her... you asked her how she felt? Hah, did you expect her to tell you the truth?
'Of course she was used to it. For the better part of two decades, she sat at the breakfast table every morning hearing her father sing her praises, calling her the brightest the family had ever seen and the 'Flora of Athopoulou', as if those words would do more to help her grow than the cystymilk on the table.
'Of course she could always let go of her past. Most of the family have left Athenius at my 'behest', but why remind her of those days when she was kept chained by training and rules? ...Even if she might not think of it the same way.
'Anyway, I've dealt with the matter. No one will bring it up ever again.
'Why? Because as a former member of the family, I hated the name Athopoulou as much as she did, that's all.'

A medic found a special notebook in the flowerbeds at the branch office, recording the common and scientific names of plants, as well as short comments written in Minoan—a little dictionary of plants, so to speak. She initially thought it was written by a child who idolized Lena, but it was Lena herself who showed up at the lost-and-found. Lena told the curious operator that she had indeed written those notes herself; however, their purpose was not so much to remember, but to forget.
Lena left Athenius years ago under unspoken pressure from her family, attempting to restart her perfuming career and botany studies elsewhere, but ran into difficulties with communication. The language and naming conventions of the Minoans were shaped by their love of poetry and stories, so without an actual physical object, it was impossible to explain to a Victorian merchant what a 'Reflection of Narcissus' was, and she had a hard time progressing her perfuming work until she memorized the names of plants in the common tongue.
'This was the most basic thing, and what I would tell any Minoan child who wanted to follow in my footsteps. But the truth is, I never spoke the names of plants in Minoan after I left my homeland... I hated them.' The operator's impression of Lena had always been one of polite gentleness. She rarely if ever recalled Lena directly expressing her like or dislike of something. Yet it seems her return to Minos—this 'home' that once rejected her—had caused her to abandon her restraint. 'The scientific naming of plants is structured and objective, reflecting a precise truth, such as their family, genus and species, their discoverer, and their characteristics. Minoan names for plants are vague and ambiguous, full of meticulous poetry. I understand its beauty as well as anyone, but I also understand how it causes people to place expectations upon those names.'
Having grown up shouldering the expectations of her family, it was fortuitous that Lena had a natural affinity for plants and nature. She gladly accepted coursework far beyond what was reasonable for a child, the massive amount of plant names and etymology she was expected to memorize, and her father's pop quizzes, all in the name of her love and passion. At the time, she did not understand the compromise that her harmonious relationship with her family was built upon. Not until she left Athenius and saw flowers from her homeland again did she realize the burden that all the names and stories of plants she memorized had become. She could no longer find it in herself to call them by the names she once knew them by.
On this return to her homeland, and in her communications with patients, Lena once again hears the stories and names of plants that she spent more than a decade memorizing. But she understands that her patients are calling to her in the same way she might instinctively say the name of a familiar plant in Minoan as she gathers herbs in the forests of Athenius alone. The burdens of the past are lifted, and she once again flips through the 'dictionary', communicating with Minoans in the words they are most familiar with. She is now able and willing to extend a helping hand.

Lena wrinkled her nose. The corridor smelled strange. She had returned briefly from the Athenius branch office, and her ride back to Minos was leaving in twenty minutes, but she smelled something burning as she passed near the Convalescent Garden. The smell was acrid and aggressive, not like ordinary fire, more like some kind of Originium Arts. An enemy attack? But there was also a familiar scent, some kind of bright and sunny flower. The names of a dozen flowers flashed across Lena's mind, but none of them seemed to be the answer. Then she heard scattered sounds coming from behind the garden's door, and the smell grew even more chaotic, without rhyme or reason. For the first time, Lena found herself at a loss as to what was happening behind the door. The unfamiliar sound and smell made her uneasy, but this was the Convalescent Garden, the garden she had built with her own two hands. Lena clutched her staff and pulled the door open sharply—
'So... it was your handiwork I smelled, Podenco?'
'Yes! It's a brand-new essence I developed while you were away!'
'Was it part of the plan to have Beanstalk's metal crab run around with various fragrances?'
'Yes! It helped hide the scent of the small cake from you. Peacake had a lot of fun too!'
'Was Flamebringer in on the surprise as well?'
'He made a charred smell as part of the disguise. Said it was repayment for the flower seeds you gave him!'
Lena shook her head, but her ears betrayed her joy at how a group of operators who had only met because of Rhodes Island and the Convalescent Garden went through all this trouble just to fool her sense of smell and give her a surprise. She blew out the candles, and found herself in no particular hurry to go back to her other home. Why not spend a little more time with her friends here in the garden?

HR and Medical were on high alert following the arrival of Xanthos on Rhodes Island. While Rhodes Island has no shortage of operators who hail from countries in conflict with each other, no one calls the Sarkaz 'devils' here, nor do Kazimierzians go for the throats of every Ursine they see. Dr. Warfarin had obtained a rare blood sample and was working overtime to study it, messing up the shifts and forgetting to make sure that Dr. Gavial was not on duty when Xanthos came in, resulting in the two of them coming into contact with one another. Xanthos is definitely cut from the same cloth as Aspasia alright! He's a solid survivor and a fighter—not as good as me of course, but good enough to survive in the desert. Too bad he doesn't want to become my subordinate, but I won't give up so easily!

By Minoan standards, Xanthos is quite reserved—stiff even. We know that Minoans love drama, as citizen-organized performances are a frequent sight on the streets of Athenius, and Minoan villages often jointly hold small drama festivals during agricultural off-seasons. Xanthos, however, seems to have little interest in it. It is not that he does not know the stories of the heroes—he responds to citations of the legends in conversations—but his own words are always brief and succinct, never quoting proverbs or fables. His upbringing may have something to do with it: Xanthos was raised in a small village in southern Minos, near the border with Sargon. Life was hard even without Sargonian raids. His father died when he was very young, and he inherited his father's work as ferryman. He spent most of his time on the river, and his emotions flowed like the river, never rising or falling by too much. But the river was also fickle, and he had to be vigilant at all times, never letting his guard down. His taciturn and cautious manner is the result of such a life. This is not to imply that he has no hobbies: he has told us that reading poetry was his way of relaxing in those rare moments of leisure. The reasoning was that poems are relatively short, and do not make you forget the time or to monitor the condition of the river. Xanthos showed some interest when I invited him to join our Poetry Club, but began to hesitate upon learning that we get together and recite poems in front of other club members, apparently not used to group activities. My praise of his speech at the First Temple of Athenius seemed to have the opposite effect, as he looked visibly uncomfortable, though I was eventually able to convince him to come. That night, we read poems that we wrote ourselves, and engaged in some impromptu group poetry. Someone brought wine, which I had reservations about, though I must admit that good wine can indeed do wonders for the atmosphere. Once we got a little tipsy, we began to sing while someone played accompaniment, ending on a high note with the climax of the Kerespereia. Xanthos sat in a corner throughout, listening quietly and touching none of the wine (most admirably!), looking somewhat out of place. He continued to attend the meetings, sitting quietly in a corner as he did the first time, saying little except nodding on occasion upon hearing a particularly well-crafted verse. He seems to prefer sentimental odes to narrative epics, and takes a particular liking to the works of a certain female poet from Antisa. It seems that his appearance belies a much more delicate nature. —Erato, in Rhodes Island Poetry Club Report

The training of a priest is a serious matter in Minos. Children found to have the proper aptitude are sent to the temples to receive education and training at the age of ten, studying with a dozen other children of the same age. They are responsible for everyday cleaning and maintenance, while also studying the classics and learning about the heroes and their associated rituals. They also have to study scientific knowledge associated with the temple, as well as accumulate management and administrative experience, all in preparation for a career in the priesthood. The process can take more than a decade, until trainees pass their exams to become full-fledged acolytes. The priests of Minos are therefore among its most talented and educated people.
When we learned that Xanthos's apprentice in Athenius was a former trainee acolyte, we began to wonder—did this mean Xanthos possessed knowledge that rivaled the temples? There was, of course, an element of self-interest in our curiosity: there are patients of every age group at Rhodes Island, including young children who had to abandon their education because of their condition, and we wanted to give them an opportunity to continue learning.
Xanthos seemed to smile wryly behind his mask.
'Lykeion knew much more than I do, in terms of professional knowledge. I dealt with issues that occurred on the river through experience and instinct, accumulated through observation and memorization, while he understood the principles behind them, and could draw on such knowledge to understand things that he had never seen before. It was practical experience that he lacked... but the real reason I took him in as an apprentice was that he needed a reason to keep living after I saved... after he contracted Oripathy. I didn't need a caregiver or companion, but he needed something to fill his life, in order to find the strength to keep going. I'm glad that he's found a new goal.'
Xanthos was humble and did not immediately agree to take on apprentices at Rhodes Island, but we have noticed that he has a way with children, guiding them to fulfill their potential while showing remarkable patience. He tells stories of heroes to crying young patients, competes with Popukar to see who can cut planks faster using a chainsaw (and his oar), and steers Bubble and Ceobe to keep the corridor clear when they are playing in the hallways. Perhaps it comes from his experience observing the river—'one can only sail far and easy by going with the flow,' in his own words—or perhaps he is simply a natural educator.

You want to know about my life in the marshes? It wasn't like what you might find in pastoral poems. Ferrying in the marshes was not like ferrying in Athenius. It was not a simple matter of going from one side of the river to the other. Our village was surrounded by the river. Essentially, we lived in the river. The river was the most important part of life in the marshes; master the river, and you master the marshes. It was formed from rainfall and meltwater from the peaks of Mt. Hymnoi. Spring was the season for planting and irrigation, as the snow began to melt and rainfall declined. I ferried people back and forth between the village and nearby small plots of farmland, separated by the river, while keeping an eye on the snowline in the distant mountains, looking out for sudden floods. Summer was when meltwater was at its highest, the busiest season for irrigation. People guided water into the fields, and harvested young reeds which were used for weaving. Autumn was the season of harvest, with increased rainfall and reduced meltwater. The crops in the fields had to be harvested quickly, and reeds that had grown hard harvested for reserves. The river was calm in winter—villagers used harvested reeds to make handicrafts, and repaired farm tools and houses, while I ferried people between our village and neighboring villages. Reeds were a frequent sight on the river, growing along the river and marshes, forming narrow passages that only those who knew the river well could navigate successfully. Only those few could ferry the others to where fins and fowlbeasts were in abundance. Reeds were versatile materials that could be woven into baskets, mats, even houses and their foundations. We used reeds to mark out areas in the river, and filled them with reed stalks to make floating plates on which we built our homes. It may seem primitive to people used to the nomadic cities, but it was flexible and adaptable to any changes in the river. When Ithakos came, he taught us how to connect these reed plates to create large public areas, upon which we built a little temple and lit a fire that belonged to us... Life was hard, and far from affluent, but it holds a special place in my heart, not only because of the memories of home and my deceased friends and relatives, but also because it was a life that was within my grasp. All I needed to do every day was to understand the river beneath me. The river has since dried up, but it continues to flow in my heart. Having lost sight of my own heart from loss, I'm trying to understand it now, trying to tame it. Perhaps this will allow me to once again grasp my own life.

The wounds that Sargon left behind in Minos have yet to fully heal, even in the nomadic city of Athenius, far from the border. Scholars continue to piece together the cultural heritage of Minos prior to the Sargonian occupation, the priests relying on a mix of legend and imagination to recreate the ceremonies and rituals of the past. Ruins of classical buildings litter the streets; few remain intact.
We do not care about that, said the Athenians. We were free. We would build a new glory with our own hands, so long as the spirit of the heroes lived on in our hearts. Athenians smiled, put on plays on the streets, and sang at temple ceremonies, as though they had forgotten the suffering of the past—until Xanthos, the dockmaster, delivered his speech to the people of Athenius at the First Temple.
We do not care, say the Athenians now. We do not care how strong our foe is, nor the price we must pay for freedom, but we will remember the hardships along the way, and remain vigilant of our foe's cunning. And we will not forget to lay a white flower at the graves of our fallen kin.

[Code Name] Ju
[Gender] Male
[Combat Experience] None
[Place of Birth] Yan
[Date of Birth] Reported as Unknown
[Race] Undisclosed
[Height] 182cm
[Infection Status]
