[Physical Strength] Excellent
[Mobility] Standard
[Physical Resilience] Excellent
[Tactical Acumen] Excellent
[Combat Skill] Standard
[Originium Arts Assimilation] Flawed

Ju, an unemployed wanderer who roams the wilderness of Yan. He has vast experience and knowledge, and his unique nature gives him considerable historical value. He is at Rhodes Island at the Doctor's invitation, serving as an engineering consultant.

A joint examination by the Medical and Engineering Departments indicates high torso density with no presence of abnormal shadows. Originium granule readings in the circulation and motor systems are within normal parameters and show no signs of activity. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Machine-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Ju's parts were calibrated and carefully reassembled during the examination.

[Coolant Originium-Crystal Density] 0.005u/L
We are happy to announce that Ju has shared his body's detailed damping data with us, providing significant assistance to the Engineering Department's maintenance work!

It took seventeen checks before Ju told us that there was no need to conduct further examinations, as the equipment was not malfunctioning. It was blatantly obvious that he just wanted to study the equipment...
—A Medical Department Operator

Ju's examination was conducted under the curious gaze of many eyes. We tried to explore his secrets, but other than basic mechanics, there seemed to be little in common between his body and modern technology. We have yet to ascertain how it works, but by his own claims, he spent much of his 'new life' wandering the farmlands of Yan—this was the truth behind the household tale of the 'machine man' that has scared many a Yanese child. Ju himself views it from a different perspective: he believes he has done a good thing by stimulating people's curiosity toward the unknown.

As Ju's body can be freely disassembled, Engineering recommended that we publish details of several incidents in order to mitigate the impact that an 'accidental' loss of parts may have on other operators.

Incident 1: An engineering operator inquired about the structure of Ju's head at their first meeting, for research purposes. Ju proceeded to remove his head and gave a detailed lecture. The operator froze for ten minutes, terminated all research into Ju, and received psychological counseling at the Medical Department.

Incident 2: During maintenance work, an operator discovered a row of fingers on the worktable and assumed that a safety incident had occurred. Ju apologized for the misunderstanding and promised to arrange the fingers in the shape of a smiley face next time to avoid unnecessary panic.

Incident 3: The Logistics Department reported that an operator found a mechanical arm on the edge of a training field early in the morning, tapping the ground rhythmically with its index finger. On-duty personnel investigated the incident after they heard the operator's screams. An investigation revealed that Ju had left his arm behind to let it watch other operators train for him and learn from their techniques when he finished the calibration checks the night before, and had forgotten to retrieve it.

[Analysis report of current data on Ju]
File Number: 0375687
Classification Level: ■■

This is an unusual investigation: the entity sitting opposite us is not flesh and blood, but a mechanical body made from countless intricate components, containing the consciousness and memories of an ancient Yanese Feranmut. Ju's form was destroyed in the war, and his current vessel was built during a time that he claims was 'insignificant'. When asked why he kept it, Ju said, 'Taking human form is one way to understand humanity.' This helped us understand the importance of Ju's principles to himself—his current form may be considered an extension of his ideals and philosophy. We can see an inkling of this from the Sui Regulator's files:
From a worldly perspective, the result of an attack is determined by victory and defeat, and that is how history is written. But Ju seeks to answer a more fundamental question: What is victory? To Ju, the nature of attack lies in a lack of mutual love. People loved themselves but not others; they loved their community, but did not care about other communities. As such, they viewed others from a perspective of pillage rather than respect, destroying cities, killing people, expanding territory, and flexing their power. But the dead do not come back to life, shattered families cannot be repaired, and trampled pride cannot be restored. The victor stands atop a mountain of bones, basking in glory earned with blood. In the course of history, war is abstracted into a conflict of interests between nations or factions, but Ju sees war through the lens of each individual victim. Children who lost their father, mothers who buried their sons, survivors despairing amongst the ruins... they are not numbers, nor pieces on a chessboard.
Ju told us, 'The victor does not love.' Indeed, he believes that anyone engaged in victory and defeat cannot love.
Ju spoke of wars that became far more than what the instigators expected—a campaign that began under the banner of justice became an indiscriminate massacre; an act of self-defense became another invasion. War has its own logic and rarely stops when the one who began it pleases. Those who partake in it become drawn into its logic, and are driven to do things they would not have under ordinary circumstances, regardless of the ideals they once held.
Based on what we know, Ju and his followers participated in several actions to stop war. These were not grand events filled with fanfare—they simply arrived on scene before the siege began and attempted to persuade the belligerents to lay down arms. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. At times, they helped poorly defended cities improve their defenses. At others, he went alone to beseech the aggressor to stop the conflict. He cares nothing for personal gain and loss, only for the hope that human dignity would not be trampled by martial strength.
For Ju, victory is not the vanquishing of the foe, but the elimination of hostility. It is not about occupying territory, but winning over people's hearts. Those who rely on violence may win this day, but they are simply setting the stage for their defeat tomorrow. The same applies to the war between humanity and Feranmut. Ju could not stop it, but at least he provided a standard to judge right and wrong, a framework for reflection. The power of thought is already being exercised if people ask themselves whether peaceful coexistence is truly a fleeting dream when they take up arms.
At the close of the meeting, Ju told us that he does not expect his ideals to change everything. He has only done what he thinks should be done, following in his own nature. His ideas are like seeds—people centuries later will not remember which seed grew into the great tree, but hope will live on as long as it exists.

In the beginning, when the primal void first gave way to order, people urgently sought peace and plenty, and the learned folks of the time traveled the land to express their convictions. Some advocated ruling through courtesy, others through law. Some said the government should be quiet and stay out of everyday life, others saw strength and strategy as the way. It was a time of chaos, yet in chaos there was vitality; a time of conflict, yet through conflict came progress. Different schools had different ideas, but all harbored the same hope of making the land a better place.
It was an era that was never seen again.

It was a time of infinite possibilities. Perhaps there was a chance for humanity to coexist peacefully with Feranmuts, but it was buried by Its will and obsession.
—Ju

The war for which Sui was responsible drove an irreparable rift between humanity and Feranmuts. New schools of thought had risen prior to the war, emphasizing defense against external threats and securing internal order, distinction between close and distant relationships, and a clearly delineated hierarchy, but all of them came down to emphasizing the existential threat that the difference between humanity and Feranmuts represented. The House of Yan is built upon the decline of the Feranmuts, and so the people must be united and order established, building consensus for the great campaign to come.
In such a climate, Ju's idea of 'universal love' was akin to heresy, scorned for being a pipe dream that ignored the realities of life and the selfishness of humanity. Meanwhile, those who were moved by Ju's ideals and became his followers continued to pursue this distant dream, despite being few in number. Stubborn and rational, they became known as the Shanhaizhong.
But being a Feranmut was a 'sin' in itself. Ju knew that he would only bring doom to his followers if he stayed with them. As the shadow of war spread to the land that he and humanity had developed together, his existence became a sword that hung above the heads of the Shanhaizhong. When war came, the Shanhaizhong lost Ju and were scattered, but they survived.
Centuries passed. The Shanhaizhong have changed. Some offshoots have faded into history, while others have drifted from their ideals over the years. Ju's teachings have become abridged, distorted, or mixed with other ideologies, becoming unrecognizable.
Ju understands the reasons for the change. Hate begets hate, and blood begets blood. 'Centuries' is a long time, enough to turn the most gentle of ideals radical... Obsession can claim even Feranmuts, never mind humans.
These people view Ju with veneration, confusion, and barely disguised disappointment. They expected a leader who would lead them to victory, but all Ju could offer was principles that had been cast aside centuries ago. He is not surprised—he knows that his ideas will never become mainstream, be it past or present.

Ju is not the only one who seeks a path of peace under heaven. Unlike Ju, Hou's ideals are only seen in fragments, often in the form of allegories that are absurd yet thought-provoking. Some see him as a cynical ne'er-do-well, others an idle hermit, but a select few see something deeper in his satire and castigation.
Every encounter between Ju and Hou has ended in a lengthy argument. Their differences seem to be fundamental—Ju advocated for active engagement with the world, changing things with universal love and non-aggression, while Hou thought that such hard work was futile, and it was better to let nature take its course and distance oneself from things.
Ju saw humans as easily deceived and prone to selfishness, and that order would eventually become the accessory of violence if humans were left to judge right or wrong based on their own preferences, turning it into a tool for the strong to oppress the weak. Only by appealing to a higher order that does not easily change can justice find its home, just as craftsmen make vessels from specifications, which in turn are born out of practice.
Meanwhile, Hou sees Ju's attempts to communicate peace through pure rationality as a source of conflict unto itself. For every person who advocates for universal love, there is another who advocates for partial love. For every person who advocates for non-aggression, there is another who advocates for conquest. The more heated the debate of right or wrong, the more chaotic things become. It would be better to forget the differences and let everything settle itself according to fate and nature.
For his part, Ju has long understood that Hou's was a path of compromise and transcendence. It demands that people set aside their obsessions and differences, to be one with heaven and earth through serenity and non-action. Fundamentally, both paths lead to harmonious coexistence, only Ju wants to overcome the barriers separating people with universal love, while Hou wants to eliminate them through transcendence. Their methods may be very different, but there has never been a dispute about each other's goals. They both know that, ultimately, their paths converge upon the same destination.
One of Hou's allegories talks about a great tree with soft and gnarled wood that was no good for building or furniture. No one bothered to cut it down because of its uselessness, and so it lived to a ripe old age, offering its vast canopy shade as shelter. He said that Ju devoted all his life to what was 'useful', such as elaborate and effective siege defense equipment, and concise teachings of a greater good, all efforts that point toward something tangible and actionable. But even the strongest walls can be breached, and the most elaborate equipment solved. The arts of siege defense may protect against one attack, but not the endless greed and hatred of man.
Siege defense equipment will no longer be necessary when people truly forsake aggression. Ju understands this, and it is precisely what he is seeking. The ideal of peace, the mentality of non-aggression, abhorrence of violence—these things can neither be built nor defended, but they are the foundation of all that is material. One is pragmatic, the other transcendent; one wants people to set aside their selfishness and love others as they love themselves; the other wants people to forget there is a difference between oneself and others. Their ideals are so different, and they will continue to think back to the sentiments that their differences created many years into the future. Those arguments only truly carry weight when they come from the mouths of the debaters.

Ju left the Shanhaizhong, but his rules remained.
The principles that he often repeated, demonstrated by example, and etched upon bamboo slips and his followers' hearts, formed an invisible barrier that continued to protect the Shanhaizhong after his departure.
When he was still there, however, the rules were alive too. They grew with his words and deeds, adapted to changing times, and could be tailored to the context. Ju was able to determine when to be strict and when to be flexible, who to trust and who to be on guard against, which principles were temporary and which were fundamental.
The rules died when he left. The Shanhaizhong carried on his teachings, living in the wilds that he made, and were unable to respond to lawless violence and unbound malice.
Principles become dogma when removed from their context. Ju's followers remembered every word he said, but not necessarily the spirit behind them. Their descendants may treat his teachings as scripture, but the message inevitably deviated from the original meaning as it was passed from one generation to the next.
Ju understood this limitation well. He could protect a city or a community, but not everything. He could teach a person or a group, but he could not ensure that his teachings were properly understood and utilized. His life is long, but not eternal. Feranmuts are powerful, but not omnipresent.
Ju has thought about whether it would have been better if they had never followed him and never formed the Shanhaizhong. Perhaps they would have found their own respective paths, and perhaps they would not have died in the name of his teachings.
But would they really have had a better fate, if they had never met him?
He does not know the answer. Maybe there isn't one.
Rules become forgotten or distorted; perhaps people need to learn to love each other by their own instincts.

I don't ask for my ideals to be remembered. It's enough to know that they have made someone suffer less and commit less evil, sometime, somewhere.
—Ju

[Code Name] Wang
[Gender] Male

[Date of Birth] Feb 2

Wang, former military advisor to Yan, now an unemployed weiqi player. Younger brother to Chongyue, and older brother to Nian, Dusk, Ling, etc. He came to Rhodes Island to recuperate at Chongyue's recommendation, and is occasionally consulted on tactical matters.

Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.00u/L
Look! The readings just went off the charts, before dropping back to zero... the instruments were working just fine a moment ago. What happened?
—Surprised Medic

...I asked the Doctor. Just write a zero.
—Warfarin, looking up at the ceiling with despondent eyes

Following the monumental event that occurred in Baizao, Nian and her siblings began to spend more time on Rhodes Island, with a marked improvement in their moods—Chongyue being the sole exception. He spent little time on the ship, only coming back to check on his siblings from time to time before setting out again.
It was during this time that Wang showed up at the reception, on an otherwise completely unremarkable afternoon.
'I would like to speak to the supervisor here,' he said.
The impression he gave was that of a quiet, peaceful, and polite man, very different from the sinister and dangerous image from the rumors.
Wang remained on Rhodes Island as a guest, and we agreed to his request not to tell his siblings. After all, Rhodes Island is much bigger now, and surely it was not so likely to accidentally run into someone... until one day Wang vanished into thin air as he was walking along a corridor. It turned out that he had walked right into a painting that Dusk had planted, and emerged an hour later with his head hanging dejectedly, followed by Nian with a gleeful smile on her face, Dusk with her eyes red, and Yu whose sleeves were wet with tears...
We do not know if Wang could have seen through Dusk's little trick, nor did we witness their reunion. All we know is that Wang stopped avoiding his family from that day forth.
Families inevitably have their little squabbles, of course. One day, someone overheard the normally carefree Ling berate Wang, saying, 'You want to hide, that's your own business, but couldn't you have had the decency to at least write to Chongyue? Have you any idea how hard he was looking for you?'
That was when Chongyue showed up and said something to her, which seemed to calm her down a little. Finally, she sighed and turned around to leave with a flick of her sleeves. No one knew whether she had let it go or meant something else.
Wang is rarely disturbed on Rhodes Island, other than for important festivals, family reunions, or when a sibling forces his dorm door open, and he rarely speaks even at such occasions other than when spoken to, seldom answering questions not from family members unless they are to his liking. He usually sits in his room, gazing at the weiqi board in front of him. It looks as though he is daydreaming, but one can plainly see his thoughts stirring in his heterochromatic eyes.

We thought he had fulfilled his dreams, but it seems like he has even more to worry about now, both for the greater good and for personal interest. He can't let either go... Bring him this rice cake. He seems to have gotten even thinner lately.
—Shu

Wang's fame as the greatest weiqi master in Yan is known to many on Rhodes Island even before his arrival, and quite a few of them can hardly resist the urge to have a game of weiqi with him. Fortunately, though he usually looks unapproachable, he rarely turns down an invitation to play weiqi. Even if he has been lost in thought just seconds before, all you need to do is knock on the door and ask if he'd like to have a game. By the time you step inside, the board is already set up.
Many operators have challenged him, but few have sniffed even a single victory—hardly surprising, considering Yu's skill in cooking and Dusk's skill in painting. Closure once tried to challenge Wang by connecting all of Rhodes Island's support robots in parallel (Friston-3 declined to participate out of dignity, but spectated the match with great interest). When faced with the choice of tapping ZOOT's reserve computing power and just pulling the circuit breaker, she wisely chose the latter.
Outside of Closure, there is someone else equally obsessed with challenging Wang, and that someone is none other than Zuo Le. Although he was no longer required to keep a close eye on the proxies, Zuo Le felt obliged to play a round with Wang. A few months later, when Grain Buds asked him about the result, he scratched his head abashedly, saying he was not yet ready. It turns out that he only knew the basics of of weiqi, and had never had the time to truly study it. Compared with Wang who had pursued the art of strategy for nearly a thousand years, he was naturally outmatched.
Finally, Nian arranged for a game between Zuo Le and Wang handicapped at nine stones in Zuo Le's favor. Unsurprisingly, Zuo Le lost handily, but there were more twists and turns than expected. Wang started out playing aggressively, but he began to tone it down once he realized that Zuo Le had no answer, nor was he attempting to duel as equals—he was simply there to learn from the superior player. Wang ended up giving Zuo Le a small spot in the corner, so that the final score would not look too bad.
Wang became less guarded against operators from Yan after this game of weiqi.

To Wang, playing weiqi with someone is like being in a fight to the death, or living together with the opponent for years. He can tell all your secrets, as well as what you're thinking. Perhaps he saw in the Candleholder's moves that Yan's current stance toward us is genuine, and was thus convinced to let down his guard. Good news, I say.
—Ling

[Classified Log]
I never thought the problem would be solved in such a manner... or at least delayed from a pressing threat to one we will not have to worry about again for another millennium or so.
'Wa Stone', 'Bu Fan', the Jingyu Prime Vein... the first Originium gave Yan the power to vassalize the gods and contain the Feranmuts, and the capital to catch up during the Crystal Age. These gifts should have blown up in Yan's face just as what happened in Ursus, but that was nullified by a Feranmut with inextricable ties to the nation. With the first Originium gone, the Jingyu Prime Vein's Originium growth rate has entered an irreversible decline, but overall, it remains far more stable than the Kolossal Prime Vein, giving Yan's industry plenty of time to transition, and helping Yan avoid the same chaos that engulfed Ursus. A stable Yan is good for the stability of Higashi, Rim Billiton, Kazdel, and Ursus as well. This does not even take into account the turmoil that was successfully avoided, the calamity that the first Orignium should have caused... He really did achieve the greater good, and bought valuable time for the land.
As natives of Terra, the paracausal nature of Feranmuts is inherently incompatible with how Originium stores information. The Feranmut will eventually succumb to the Originium, but until then, there is no safer box than the interior of a Feranmut for storing Orginium and cutting it off from its controller.
This does not come without a price, of course. Kroos's report, official Yanese communications, and Ju's statement all indicate that it took all of Ya's lifeforce to plant the first Originium into the bestial Sui. In addition, whatever consciousness it is that is now in control of the bestial Sui will suffer from extreme, unbearable, endless pain.
Wang as he is on Rhodes Island is currently no more than a weiqi stone. I'm not saying he's incomplete—after all, these are Feranmuts we are talking about, and the Wang we see is certainly Wang in his entirety. What I'm saying is that, as he plays weiqi with you, he is also being constantly tormented deep beneath Baizao, which explains the abnormal crystal density readings from his checkup: at times, it was the weiqi stone you saw; at others, it was the Feranmut, slowly but surely crystallizing from the wound.

[Audio Log]
The writing knife?
Do not ask me. It does not belong to me. It is none of my business that she entrusted it to Jun, who entrusted it to the young lady. There is only one thing that I regret about the knife, and I found the answer in the Tomb of Sui.
As for the powers of the knife... most of us do not intentionally create objects of power, with the exception of Nian. The objects associated with us came to be as a result of our influence over a long period of time, just like It unconsciously created the geists from inside Its tomb... It would not have suffered mundane wine cups, paperweights, and cutlery to be imbued with the power of evolution too, if It were awake and aware.
Yes, this box for storing weiqi stones is similar to the writing knife. Once, it was no more than an ordinary box. The influence of Sui caused it to take the form of a beast a century ago, making it the perfect container for the hundred and eighty-one black stones. All the stones are gone now, save for the one in front of you, but it sought me out after my awakening and would not leave my side after it found me, so I allowed it to stay.
Let us speak of things that are truly worth our time. I do not need your hollow praise—all I want to know is who made Originium, and who is trying to take away everything that Originium gave to this land. What is their ultimate goal, and how will it affect me and my family?
(Recording interrupted)
...I appreciate your candor.
I will continue my calculations based on the information you provided. Come to me immediately if there is any new development.
Why do I do this?
I believe my siblings have already told you the answer, or demonstrated it through action. For my part, I have unfinished business—
You wish to help?
...
That's enough talk. We can continue the game if you want to play. If you've had enough, surrender, and we'll do it another day.

'A beast shrinks long and lone. A miser's shadow cold.
It takes its number second. Black and white at odds.
Finds solitude in stone. It dwells on countless paths.
But its schemes are finite. Desolate out and in.
Alas, alack. Its stones could be no gems, its wood is no fine grain.
All thought and schemes. It seeks a life in death.
How could it not know? A part fights the whole, defying the land's law. It may endure awhile, yet peril will come.
It writhes and wracks in ruin. Its spirit thin, it leaves its kin, it takes rebuke.
It breaks its flesh; now the tide is turned. A thousand years; the wish is fulfilled.
Now scattered to the winds like mist. Haze waters far and still.
Through the turning of day and night, between heaven and earth, only cold stones and a broken board.'

The text of the rubbing is often corrupted in its frequent transcriptions. At the time of the most recent comparison, a slow yet irreversible change was found to have already begun in the stele's physical material.

avgList.storyIntro: There are still people waiting for you... Not just one. Many.

Ch'en, former Lungmen superintendent and former head of the L.G.D.'s Special Inspection Unit, graduated from the Victorian Royal Guard Academy with superb marks and outstanding achievements. During her time with the Department, she cracked down on crime, fought violent offenders, tracked down armed fugitives, and brought down international criminals.
Having resigned from the L.G.D., she is now officially a member of Rhodes Island. In accordance with her wishes, she is mainly assigned to provide field operators adequate support and on-location guidance.
She continues to fight on the frontlines as a Rhodes Island Operator.

Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Small traces of crystallization are visible on Operator Ch'en's body surface.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.21u/L

Ch'en's condition has deteriorated since her last checkup. We know her resolve and understand her reasons, but she must take better care of herself...
—Sussurro

You know how she is. Oripathy or not, she'll never listen.
—Warfarin

'Broken shields have been melted down into plowshares. The fire in the furnace has changed.
'The name Reunion is increasingly used to refer to a village, rather than a group of Infected.
'Oversight? I have my duty as an operator of Rhodes Island, but this is also a personal commitment for me. What is different about Nine's 'fairness'? What judgment will Talulah receive? Will a reborn Reunion truly light a lasting fire of hope in the snowstorm? Someone must bear witness, and it should be me. It must be me.'

Following the Londinium incident, Ch'en traveled throughout Ursus, from the disputed region at the Ursus-Kazimierz Border, to the Grypherburg region, to the distant north... We later learned that Ch'en operated like a Messenger, braving martial law, harsh weather, and magnetic storms to cross the tundra, establishing the basic framework of an intelligence network for Rhodes Island. Outside of the task force that the Doctor and Amiya personally led, Ch'en was our most reliable and stable source of information in the Ursus region. Ch'en's aptitude in intelligence gathering, already on display in Lungmen, provided invaluable help to Rhodes Island.

[Classified Log]
Ch'en did not conceal the fact that she met with Talulah's group, witnessing them unite a group of Infected on the tundra and establish a village by the name of Reunion. To Reunion, she was candid about her role, exercising oversight in her personal capacity, procuring necessary supplies, and sharing some Rhodes Island-compiled intel with them... Her stance raised some concerns amongst the operators—when the one we need to trust is the controversial figure at the heart of the Chernobog Incident, any interaction should be subject to greater scrutiny.
In the end, we gave Ch'en our tacit approval after extensive discussion. Ch'en has undoubtedly become an important and trustworthy member of Rhodes Island, demonstrating her oversight responsibility with concrete action, and helping the new Reunion take crucial first steps toward winning trust.

'The children look forward to Hui-chieh's visits. Although supplies are never plentiful, they have been learning to sew teddy bears because they think she loves them after she was seen gazing at a teddy bear, lost in thought.'
'I know a lot of the resources and news that Ch'en brought came from Rhodes Island, and I understand your reservations about me. I can't guarantee that there will be a perfect ending, nor do I expect us to truly understand one another, but I guarantee that Reunion will not repeat its old mistakes. Your torch is not the only one that burns bright. There are those who carry it into the darkest night, so that it may illuminate others.'

A great snowstorm struck many places in Yan, the likes of which had not been seen for a century. The snow lasted months, covering the land in white, and making the bright red figure traveling upon it particularly conspicuous. Rumors speak of a swordswoman who has been journeying across the land since last year, fighting for justice with her sword. She helped rebuild ruined houses in Baizao, punished bandits in Danyan, and cleared clogged water channels in Jiangqi... is she on some sort of quest? There are many differing opinions: some say she often asked those she helped where the local library was, and infer that she was seeking some secret tome that would allow her to break through a bottleneck in her training; others have seen her visit cemeteries, and believe her to be following the trail of a departed friend; and others claim that she often visited the sites where schools and colleges once stood, and hypothesize that she is a Tianshi, sent by the Ministry of Rites to investigate ancient sites... The only consensus is that there is no consensus. Some martial arts schools claimed her to be one of their students, only for the claim to be immediately shot down—'You're full of crap! She doesn't even know your dialect. How could she have studied there for decades?' Others have tried to challenge her to a duel. The first challenger recalls that she readily accepted his challenge, but he was stunned when she spoke a line straight out of a kung fu film. She was clearly unfamiliar with the modern-day martial arts landscape of Yan. Subsequent challengers were no longer met with the same flowery lines. My investigation indicates that our heroine has moved north, and it remains to be seen whether we will see her emerge in Dahuang or Lungmen next. I would like to close this column with a word of advice... challenging her is really not for the faint of heart, or anyone who is not supremely confident in their skills! —Excerpt from Jianghu Monthly, Issue 02, 1103 [Classified Log] Ch'en's request for field assignment in Yan is hereby approved. The Tomb of Sui incident carries tremendous significance for both Yan and Terra as a whole. For Yan, it meant the resolution of a thousand-year affliction; for Terra, it was a relief to know that the Jingyu Prime Vein was not being depleted at nearly the same rate as the Kolossal Prime Vein, even though neither Rhodes Island nor Yan has been able to conclusively determine the current state of the first Originium. That does not mean, however, that Yan can fully escape this Terra-wide crisis. We had not previously made any association between Ch'en's matter and that of the Feranmuts. It was only when her identity and her 'family matter' became known to us that we realized her 'family matter' was, essentially, the family matter of Yan... Ch'en did not return to Yan's center of power following the resolution of the crisis at Baizao, instead opting to wander the lands in search of traces of a departed Sui proxy. Her reasons for taking up this responsibility are clearly linked to the writing knife that she obtained during her trip to Baizao. 'From Baizao to Shangshu, to Yumen and Lungmen... from south to north, from the heartlands to the frontiers, I discovered many traces that the proxy left behind. If she managed to bring writing and history to such distant lands back then, perhaps the land of fairness and justice we are seeking really does exist after all.'

In the reports about the Tomb of Sui incident that the Yanese operators submitted, nothing caught our attention more than the account of Ch'en stopping Yumen with a single swing of her sword. According to Zuo Le, Ch'en cut power to all of Yumen in an instant using nothing more than a tiny writing knife, buying crucial time for him to neutralize the remaining artillery positions. Nian's account, on the other hand, was rather different: 'She was muttering something like As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast, then there was a gust of sandstorm, and then Yumen just stopped. What do you mean my statement was as vague and incomprehensible as my films? You can ask the others if you don't believe me—did you hear that, Shu? They don't believe me!' Her shouting caught the attention of the other Yanese operators present. Mr. Nothing heard the story, waved his fan, and walked away with a profound expression on his face. It took only a few days for the legend of how Ch'en stopped Yumen with a single swing to spread throughout Rhodes Island. And so, the next time Ch'en returned to Rhodes Island and walked into the training room, she saw every pair of curious eyes in the room fixated on her... After learning what had happened, Ch'en agreed to do a demonstration in the outdoor training grounds. But she did not draw Chi Xiao—instead, she made the gesture of a sword with her fingers, turned her wrists, stepped forward, lowered her shoulder, and swung upwards lightly—there was no breathtaking aura, but the wind began to blow, stirring up sand and dust. A few seconds later, the sandstorm cleared, and the clouds parted to reveal the sun. It took a little while for the spectators to process what had just happened. The move seemed utterly unremarkable, yet clearly extraordinary. What made it so powerful? No one dared ask, seeing the solemn expression on Ch'en's face. Observing from the side, Qiubai and Yun Qingping revealed the secret— 'It was like a ray of light breaking through the clouds, but still connected to the soil on the ground.' 'My master once said that mindset was the most important thing to the Chi Xiao style. The swing just now was very different from the traditional finishing move of Chi Xiao. If the philosophy of Lord Wei's sword is to strike with no regret, Miss Ch'en's sword represents the admission and acceptance of regret, to press forward regardless of regret.' 'That's what makes Ch'en different from Chief Wei.' 'What's that supposed to mean? Did you understand a word of that, stinking rat?' '...There was already a hint of that move in her sword when she was in Yumen.' 'Yumen? She was in Yumen when you were there? ...Hey, why aren't you saying anything? Why are you walking away? Did you really understand that? Wait up!' 'Take it easy, Missy—the move sends the message that Ch'en never gives up partway.' As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast. Never fear, never waver, long though the journey be. The light shines through when the clouds part. One must overcome the obstacles of one's own heart to fully comprehend the way of the sword. The sword begins and ends with the heart, but the spirit of the sword lingers. Those who fail to act because something seems impossible shall lose their spirit, and their sword lose its soul. —This segment has been rewritten many times; Ch'en says she is still working on it

As Ch'en sent back more and more reports during her time in Ursus, we set up a dedicated storage area for them at the Doctor's suggestion. Reviewing these reports made us realize just how long Ch'en has been with us. From Summary of Conditions in Lungmen Slums and Tripartite Investigation Report of the Governments of Dossoles and Bolívar, to Development of Law and Order in Columbia and Challenges in Implementation and Overview of Victorian Dukes and Tara, to the recent reports on Ursus and Yan, these are not just raw intelligence collected by Ch'en, but also focused and astute observations and commentaries made by someone embarking on a long journey. They are of great significance to both Rhodes Island and Ch'en herself. The fact that Ch'en is part of Yan's imperial bloodline is no longer a secret on Rhodes Island, but she has not been shunned or approached because of it. Perhaps it is because she has already left a deep impression fighting alongside the others as a former Lungmen cop, or perhaps it is because the significance of her bloodline pales in comparison to her experiences across Terra. While Ch'en keeps her distance from the Yanese government, it does not mean she no longer cares about the country. She has never truly left Yan—or rather, she has never truly left Lungmen. She is still searching for a land of fairness and justice, and she hopes that she will find it in the soil that she stands upon, but she is not bound by this land, nor by any other. For us, the most valuable thing about Ch'en has never been her position, but her will and direction. She does not belong entirely to Rhodes Island, but her goal of seeking a land of fairness and justice aligns closely with Rhodes Island's mission. Operators who have gone on field missions with her say that there is a sort of certainty about Ch'en that is reassuring—she understands what she is seeking, and has never wavered. While the concepts of fairness and justice may differ somewhat from language to language and context to context, they ultimately point toward the same conviction: a belief in a better tomorrow. We all believe that Terra will become better than it is today. 'Officer Ch'en—no, Ch'en is our comrade and kindred spirit, one of Rhodes Island's most important partners. Of that there is no doubt. Elite operator? Ahem... she understands what she wants all too well, and our paths will not necessarily always be aligned—of course, a consistent presence at headquarters or squad operation has never been a criterion for elite operator selection... Perhaps you could ask her yourself the next time she comes back?'

I saw a village burned to the ground in the north. The charred remains stood out in the white snow. There were signs of fighting, and bodies of both uninfected and infected people. I'm not sure what happened there.
Are such scenes a regular sight in Ursus?
Did you see the same thing when you were in Ursus, all those years ago?

Received communication from Rhodes Island. Something has happened to the Doctor's team. HQ has sent a special task force to Ursus, and I have a feeling you'll run into them again.
Security is really tightening in the Far North. I was thoroughly questioned and searched just walking into an ordinary hotel today.
There are a lot of movements from many different directions. I do not yet have a clear view... but I'll get to the bottom of it.

Received a letter from Madam Fumizuki yesterday...
The events in the Far North were just the beginning. Ursus is facing an even greater crisis. If the events truly have implications across all of Terra, as the Doctor predicted, Yan will not stand idly by, and Wei Yenwu certainly will not. He will do something.
Should I...

Back in Victoria, you encouraged me to do what I had already made up my mind to do. I found you again, but we still do not know the truth. Mother, your father, that pathetic man, and Wei Yenwu... We should have been told the truth about what happened. We have a right to know. Perhaps you don't care anymore, but I can't cast it aside so easily.
Someone told me that those old folks were young and ambitious once. What happened to them? Their ambitions grew rusty, and the only thing they have left is silence, keeping them from telling the truth... I must go back, to Lungmen, to Baizao. If they will not tell the truth, I will find it myself.
I ran away many times, but I don't plan on running away forever—you didn't run away either, did you?
Heaven burned red over Grypherburg that night... the fire on the ground burned for a long time. Buildings were collapsing, and other things were collapsing with them. The stubborn stone split apart in the fire, and light shone out through the crack... I still see the fire when I close my eyes, and it gives me the courage to walk toward the truth.
I think I'm ready. I'm going back.
...Can you hear it, Tal?
I'm going back.

Two pieces of equipment carried by Taraxacum caught the attention of other operators during weapon registration. An inspection revealed the detailed designs of their components: the core unit of the 'Medicine Pot' casting staff was sculpted in the style of ancient Sargonian jewelry, while the medicine storage equipment in the shape of a dandelion seed head is reminiscent of portable medical equipment used on the battlefield. The three decorative chimes seem to originate from a market near the borders of Yan, and the skateboard that can briefly fly while carrying a person was clearly inspired by trending Columbian flying machines. It took a few days for Engineering to ascertain the two weapons' safety—meanwhile, inquiries with local branches reveal an exact match between the parts' places of origin, and Taraxacum's self-report of his recent travels. Surprisingly, this young Kuranta boy has already journeyed across almost half of Terra with his teacher. We were even more surprised by his statement that he carries his jet skateboard in order to deliver medicine to patients more quickly. We believed his story because he always seemed serious about things, until we saw him excitedly sign up for the on-deck capture-the-flag game, only to be forced to forfeit when his skateboard malfunctioned. The real kicker is that he snuck into the kitchen after the competition and devoured five servings of Yanese barbecue, paying no heed at all to the healthy eating that he normally preaches... Maybe the kid just likes to skate. Say, did he go off to take lessons from Aciddrop again? Apparently, both were gifts from his Yanese teacher, so he has to try to maintain them himself when his teacher's not around. Seems like a pretty trendy teacher, if he can make a jet skateboard. But Taraxacum also said his teacher was old... Well, he's probably a trendy old guy, like Chongyue. —On-duty Engineering Operator

Taraxacum's favorite haunt is the hospital. Medical Department staff told us that Taraxacum was not particularly impressive when he first arrived: his medical knowledge was quite haphazard, causing concerns for the department head. But he demonstrated outstanding aptitude when it came to practical work, and was easily able to follow Dr. Warfarin's instructions, even when she was using technical jargon. We learned that this was the result of his instruction under his mentor. According to Taraxacum, his teacher rarely spoke or gave him systematic instruction in medical knowledge, but always took him along on patient visits, giving him the opportunity to observe and learn. Taraxacum was also periodically given a thick stack of ancient Yanese medical books, telling him to study them himself and ask questions if there was anything he did not understand. Taraxacum gradually grew into the role of assistant, and accumulated considerable clinical experience, though his education was somewhat antiquated by the standards of modern systematic medicine. It seems his teacher Fāng, younger brother of Nian's, shares a few common features with Dusk, especially when she first came to Rhodes Island. Was Dr. Fāng a reclusive hermit, just like Dusk? 'What's my master like? I guess he does sound like the kind of reclusive sages you find in Yanese dramas, but he's actually quite familiar with modern medical technology and equipment! Then why am I so unfamiliar with the medical department's instruments? Well... I don't get a lot of chances to see new stuff, always being on the road with my master! Besides—' He strokes the beard that he does not have. 'Master Fāng said: You haven't even mastered the basic Yanese medical books yet. The newer stuff can wait...'

[From the Candleholder Archives] July 1st, 9am The proxy has entered Sargon, providing basic medical assistance to villages he passed. No unusual activity. July 21st, 9pm The proxy has entered the northwest desert, where a small Catastrophe had recently struck. Fāng is looking for survivors... The boy has recovered. As for the others... there is little time left for them. Fāng has done all that he could, giving the boy a chance to say goodbye to his family. September 23rd, 6pm The proxy has left the village, but the boy continues to follow and cannot be persuaded to turn back. It is not my place to judge their actions... but Fāng has seen the same scene too many times, even during my tenure as his Candleholder alone. He must not allow his compassion to run unchecked. He cannot help everyone... On the other hand, there are no other survivors in the village. Could the boy really survive in this desert, if he does not follow Fāng? October 26th The proxy has tacitly consented to the boy following him. His true intentions are unknown at this time. No irregularities were found. Feng Xu's personal statement is attached: I... I just didn't know what to do. I simply wanted to survive, no matter what... I'll drive carts and pick herbs for you and Master. I'll do anything... anything that I can help with! ...Are you Master's bodyguard? You follow him all the time, but hardly ever talk to him... It is almost time for me to retire, though my heart is at ease, knowing that there will be someone there to take care of Fāng... Feng Xu is almost as tall as Fāng now. 'Thank you for everything.' —Comment in a corner of the page

Operator Bellone's first visit to Rhodes Island caused a small uproar within HR, as we had previously written in Operator Vigil's file that Vigil was the 'last leader of Siracusa's Bellone Family'.
This misunderstanding was quickly cleared up: according to Operator Bellone's statement, the Bellones almost dissolved when Don Bernando died, and his heir Vigil left the old city to build Nuova Volsinii. The Family's power structure had fallen apart, and the remaining former Bellones were barely scraping by under pressure from other Families, unable to either return to a normal life or join another family and thus betray Bellone. That was when Demetri Certaldo decided to take up the mantle of the Don of the Bellone Family, taking those who had lost the family's protection under his wing.
Based on our current understanding of Siracusa, we are aware that his statement is missing quite a few details. Someone who was not the designated heir could hardly have inherited a family—even a declining one—without facing opposition both within and without. When asked about this, however, he deflected our questions with a smile.
'I grew up in the famiglia. The people there are like blood family to me, and I could never abandon them no matter what,' he said, and declined to elaborate further.
It is perhaps worth mentioning that Bellone ran into Chiave's gang at lunch that day. The always-jolly Chiave welcomed Bellone's arrival with his gang—to Bellone's apparent surprise, though he eventually assented to Chiave's eager (and rather physical) show of friendship with a smile. The scene seemed familiar, but also quite different from when Vigil first arrived.
An operator who was present recalled, 'It makes you realize how easy-going Vigil is by comparison. The smile never left Bellone's face, but for some reason I was really worried for Chiave the entire time.'

The Bellone Family staked a foothold in Nuova Volsinii through the Saluzzo Vino winery. Soon after Demetri Bellone and Alberto's deal, Alberto was arrested, and control of Saluzzo Vino fell into Bellone's hands. He has since made Saluzzo Vino stronger, establishing a dominant position in the local wine market following the Kazimierz-sponsored Red Wine Championship, and demonstrating the ability to compete with international brands from outside Siracusa.
In addition to wine, the Bellone Family has also invested in various industries in Nuova Volsinii, which are also growing at a breakneck pace. Although public data is not available, it is estimated that they are bringing the Bellone Family roughly the same revenue as Saluzzo Vino, perhaps even more. Yet there are also issues: most of these investments are in traditional mafia industries such as restaurants, bars, hotels, and moneylending—rarely involving the production of physical goods—inevitably leading to speculation that the Bellone Family is going back to the old ways in Nuova Volsinii. Furthermore, while Bellone's new investments are heavily staffed with Bellone members, Saluzzo Vino maintains a strong Saluzzo presence. Even setting aside potential problems caused by mafia members in corporate leadership, one cannot help but feel concerned as to whether the Saluzzo members truly accept Bellone leadership, and whether this arrangement will impact Rhodes Island's partnership with the Bellone Family.
An HR operator made a secret visit to Saluzzo Vino with these concerns in mind.
'Signor Bellone? He's a good man!
'We're still called Saluzzo Vino, aren't we? He said Saluzzo's only working with Bellone on a temporary basis. We're still Saluzzo, of course, and he even praised us for our loyalty, saying he was honored to be working with a famiglia like ours that respects tradition!
'Of course, we're in Nuova Volsinii now, and Signor Bellone told us to respect City Hall's policies, work hard, and follow the rules of the New Urban Management Act. I can tell you it took some getting used to. Back in the day, whenever I heard my terminal ring, the first thing I did wasn't pick up the call, but check my knife and gun. But I'm not even doing any brawling these days. I work fixed hours and go home for dinner with my wife and kids. I've got to admit, it's not such a bad feeling after all.
'Oh, of course I'm still part of the famiglia. We're all waiting for Don Saluzzo to get out of prison! I even asked Signor Bellone if there was a way to get him out. He said it would be hard to get his sentence reduced under the New Urban Management Act, but he would pull a few strings and make things more comfortable for him. Sure enough, when I visited the Don a couple of days ago, he had a cell to himself and seemed to have gotten a little plumper. I'm so grateful to Signor Bellone!
'I wasn't able to talk to the Don too much in the allotted time, so I just told him about how things had been going with us. He didn't say anything, but ended the visit with a smile. I'm sure he's very grateful to Signor Bellone too!'
The HR operator could not help but feel that something was not quite right. Seeing the Perro's bright smile, however, he could only follow Alberto Saluzzo's lead and smile back.

We are well aware that Demetri Certaldo was not groomed to become the next Don of the Bellone Family. His father had held an advisor position in the Bellones, and when he was killed in a mafia struggle, young Demetri was taken in by the Family and raised alongside Operator Vigil. This sort of arrangement is in line with what we know about Siracusan mafia tradition: having core members live together helps instill loyalty in those pegged for important Family positions in the future.
Demetri quickly accepted his role as Leontuzzo's advisor, taking care of his daily needs and teaching him everything he knew about the mafia, business, and fighting—essentially grooming the boy four years his junior to become the perfect leader, one who could take care of every member of the Family and protect their interests.
This should have ensured a smooth transition of power to Leontuzzo, until Bernardo's views on the Family began to change and he brought Lavinia—Operator Penance—into the Bellone Family. Under Lavinia's influence, Leontuzzo began to deviate from the path that Demetri had set for him. This was seen as a regrettable development, but an understandable one: for Leontuzzo, the scope of the 'family' had grown from a single Family to what is today all of Nuova Volsinii, and perhaps eventually all of Siracusa. The rules of the Family that he used to value had became the law and justice that Lavinia upheld.
Again, Operator Bellone's statement here seemed to omit many details, which we do not feel the need to delve deeper into, but there was a question we could not help but ask regarding Siracusan mafia tradition: is the Family's advisor normally expected to take care of the Don's daily needs?
Bellone did not answer.
We did, however, receive a valuable reference from another 'party concerned':
'Most advisors don't, but Demetri and I grew up together. He was a few years older, and he was used to taking care of me, while I was used to being taken care of. Or maybe... he was already showing his potential to become the Don, by seeing me as his famiglia and finding it perfectly natural that he should take care of me. He used to tell me that a Don should take care of his famiglia. I think he's doing a fine job of it.'

The announcement of the amendment to the New Urban Management Act sent shock waves throughout Nuova Volsinii. Most heavily impacted were the foreign corporations in the involved industries, whose stakeholders and investors expressed their dissatisfaction to City Hall. When Bellone finally stood before Signora Sicilia, he felt nothing but fear.
It was not her power that he feared. On the contrary, when he stood before her and saw her face clearly for the first time, he saw her sagging cheeks and sunken eye sockets, and the spots on her skin that not even heavy powdering could disguise. That was when he realized that the legends of Signora Sicilia he was so familiar with took place sixty years ago, and that the legendary matriarch had already entered her twilight years.
Her gaze was still strong, her movements elegant and confident, and her words soft yet impossible to refute or defy. The authority of Siracusa was still concentrated in her, but this only served to amplify his fear: all this power was centered on her, yet she was merely mortal. The order that she represented, the influence she wielded over the many Siracusan famiglie, and the deterrence her presence represented to other countries would all inevitably vanish upon her death. When the time came, would the famiglie still sit together and negotiate in the Grey Hall to resolve their conflicts? Or would Siracusa fall into chaos and desolation again?
'I don't give a damn what happens to Siracusa after I die,'
Signora Sicilia said as she ascended the steps of her manor. Her steps were slow, and seemingly steady, but she grabbed Bellone's arm with such strength that all he could say in response was, 'Please do not mention that word, Signora. You still have many years ahead of you.'
'The only people who love to bring up that word are the young who've never known death and the old for whom death is near. I know my own body best,' she smiled. 'The future does not belong to me. Whether it belongs to you—all of you—depends on you. Your idea is interesting, and you have shown respect by coming to see me before you act. Go. Go and try it out in Nuova Volsinii.'
His fear prevented Bellone from answering, but in that instant the faint notions in his mind became concrete and firm. He had wanted someone to show him a path he could simply follow. Now, he had to become the one leading the way, the one who saw it through to the end. He must build a new order.
There is little time left. For him, for them, and for Siracusa.

One consistent theme from our interviews with members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra was that many of them had begun to identify themselves as Nuova Volsinians, or more specifically as 'members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra of Nuova Volsinii'.
Most of them came to Siracusa as exiles from Leithanien, harboring both bitterness towards Leithanien and wariness towards Siracusa. They struggled in Siracusa's cities despite their talents in music and Arts, and many even gave up on music. After all, music that was rejected by Leithanien would not necessarily fare much better in Siracusa. It was only when Paola Memminger brought them together that they finally found their home.
After her death, the members faced uncertainty about more than just personnel or venue, but also about their own futures. They mentioned that, for the first time, they were faced with the reality that without a steady anchor holding it all together, they could dissolve and scatter at any moment. Leaving was always a realistic option.
Things changed when Ripresa took over.
She did not attempt to define the orchestra's identity, nor did she emphasize to its members what they ought to represent. She simply performed the duties that seemed mundane, but were very important: ensuring that rehearsals continued on schedule, checking the details of their rental agreements with venues, and making contingency plans to avoid potential conflict. As things began to settle down, something changed subtly in the mentality of the members, nudging them towards putting down roots in the city. The members offered various answers when we asked the reason, but they all pointed to the same thing: Liesel was here, and she would conduct them tomorrow.
Notably, this shift in identity did not come from any clear gesture of acceptance by the city, but from the orchestra itself. For its members, 'Schwarzervorhang' was no longer just a collection of musicians, but a community they lived in, one in which they did not have to explain where they came from, nor constantly prepare for where to go next.
For what was perhaps the first time since they left Leithanien, the people who came together because of Paola had a home, one that they did not need to check on constantly, and one that was not easily lost. All thanks to the leadership of Paola's foster daughter.

Sonya Mikhailivna could hardly have expected the twists and turns their journey would take when she and the rest of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group signed their off-boarding checklists in the summer of 1101.
The road to Ursus was not nearly as smooth and steady as the temperature in the car. It did not take long for them to reach their first stop: the snow-covered land of Kjerag.
Zima recalls that Leto wasted little time in dropping off their tagged luggage at the station before taking the group on a tour of Kjerag's favorite tourist spots, disturbing numerous communal burdenbeasts basking in the sun with their rowdy shouting. Instructor Dur-nar had tried to warn them to stay away from the cliff to no avail. In the end, she had to tie them to her with safety ropes. For Zima, however, it was the departure that left the deepest impression. When the station staff came bearing the bill for luggage storage, Leto simply signed the name 'Paleroche' and said, 'Hand out the presents for me.' As the train departed the station, Leto laughed her ass off at the tall figure standing on the platform with chagrin on his face. When she finally stopped laughing, she told Zima that the 'presents' were not just the junk she had intended to throw away from the start, but also the warm clothing and snacks intended for the journey.
As such, when the USSG arrived in Grypherburg, the first thing they did was not submit their university applications, but purchase clothing. Zima never forgot her mission for Rhodes Island, even as she began her studies at a Grypherburg university. A prognostic sense of anxiety and excitement had come over Grypherburg society. Changes in foreign countries had become evidence for various ideologies, and everyone wanted to have a voice in Ursus's future. She felt that public opinion in Grypherburg was too complex and too far removed from the realities of everyday life. Accompanied by Instructor Dur-nar, she began to travel to nearby nomadic cities and settlements whenever school was not in session, investigating how the people there lived, what problems they faced, how they saw things, and whether their opinions were homegrown or had come from abroad.
But Zima's investigation was cut short by the incident in the Far North. The empire quickly cracked down on public opinion, the Armies' battleships were on the move, and snow had begun to fall across Ursus... Zima brought her thoughts and insights from that period back to Grypherburg. Little did she imagine that it would be far more than the Student's Assembly awaiting her.

The conclusion of the Katorga Incident did little to mitigate the tension in Grypherburg. If anything, it has intensified. For the people of Grypherburg, some of the changes were visible. The power supply had become even more inconsistent, Katorga Raion was still firmly attached to Grypherburg's power deck—though white smoke had begun to rise from a few chimneys—and the fallen statue of Igor Velikiy lay untouched, just like the broken walls. No one repaired it, no one scrawled graffiti on it, and no one even dared glance at it as they passed. Meanwhile, other changes happened beneath the surface. Zima and the Ursus Student Self-Government Group were not charged with any offenses—their actions seemingly covered up by certain parties—and they were unable to travel with Crownslayer to where Gummy's parents were located. Amiya spoke directly to Zima and Gummy to explain, while the Doctor personally signed the documents appointing Zima as director of Rhodes Island's Grypherburg office. [Audio Log] 'I understand Rhodes Island's current circumstances. The company stands out in Ursus like a drop of blood on the snow, and is in no position to openly establish a communications network or send large numbers to Grypherburg. That's what makes our work even more important. The Grypherburg office needs more than a location—but yes, thanks for cleaning the rehearsal rooms, Gummy—we need funding and connections. We need something to keep the nobles from coming after us. We need a front business, as well as reception and communication staff, and we need to do all of this ourselves. Sounds tough, doesn't it? Thankfully, we have some experience in these matters, and we all have our own strengths... Wait, you want to be the receptionist? No, Ukusik, anyone but you! We wouldn't last a week if—say, who let you in anyway? This meeting was supposed to be private! Oh no you don't, you're not getting away when you've already heard our secret. You better sign this application form here and now... Uh, we're not breaking any rules, are we, Istina? Good.' Look, I'm busy enough as it is—I'm just going to mail in this brief report, because I don't have the time. You have no idea how much trouble it is to register and operate a pharmaceutical company branch in Grypherburg! Just today, we got a notice that the fire safety inspection had been rescheduled because of a violation. We spent the whole day trying to find it. Guess what it was? That big hamaxe of mine, which was apparently 'too frightening' and therefore unsafe—what kind of nonsense is that? You'd never guess how we dealt with it either. We found a glass case, put it over it, and called it an exhibit. And guess what? It was approved. Somehow. Honestly, if I'd known this would be such a pain in the ass, I'd have taken my hamaxe to ■■■■ and picked a few fights instead! —Operator Zima's 'brief report'

A particular conversation occurred between Zima and Istina. They both independently reported it to Medical, for their respective psychological health records. I was never good with words. I wasn't sure what I was going to say, even as I opened my mouth. So I told Istina about Katorga, about what I went through in there, and she told me what she went through on the outside. I told her about what happened to Leonid, about how Faddey opposed the rescue of our fellow students, about how angry I was and how I wanted to punch him and go do my own thing. But I didn't. At the time, I thought, 'what would Istina do if she were here?' I didn't know. Maybe she would've already come up with four or five reasons to shut those mudak up, but she wasn't there. I resisted the urge to swing my fist or slap him. I forced myself to calm down and solve the problem like Istina would. I couldn't spin my words like she could, so I spoke slowly and talked about my most resolute beliefs, trusting that they would convince the others as well. Looking back, I think I did the right thing. But did I? That's what I asked Istina. I said I kind of regretted not slapping Faddey. She said she was glad, but not because of what I did. Because I regretted it. She said that proved that deep in my heart, I was still determined to be myself. I didn't know what she meant. It sounded like she was mocking me, but part of me agreed with her. For whatever reason, I even feel a little touched when I think back to that conversation with her. —Interview with Operator Zima 'Touched'? No, not at all. I wouldn't have even been locked in the kitchen prep room with Sonya if she hadn't felt the need to steal the cupcakes Instructor Dur-nar was baking. It was the most embarrassed I'd felt in a long while, having the instructor come free the two of us 'thieves' when she heard the alarm. As for what she said... I did say that, but I was not mocking her. When I did what I did outside Katorga, I often forced myself to step into Sonya's shoes, and asked myself what she would do if she were there. And just like her, I have regrets. But regret doesn't mean we did anything wrong, it's simply a reaffirmation of our self-identity. Sonya could have let loose her slap, of course, and I didn't have to force myself to do those things. But who can say whether the things we didn't do would have been better or worse? At least we're asking ourselves the question. That's good enough. There was something else I didn't get to say to Sonya, who left as soon as the instructor arrived. I'm sure you're aware that some things are hard to say once the moment has left us, so I thought I might as well say it here: I'm glad we both chose to affirm who we are, Sonya. I think that's why we trust each other. —Interview with Operator Istina They'd gone through almost the entire batch of cupcakes by the time I arrived. It's all good, though. This is why I like baking. —Operator Dur-nar

We brought down those mudak. We are free. Now we must gather people, everyone who would join us, and show Grypherburg who its true master is! —Words on a page I saw the people whimpering in pain. I saw the scarred soil. Not another drop of milk could be squeezed from it, yet the greedy nobles and vile bureaucrats continue to torment it like leeches, torment our motherland. I must resist. I must take up the sword! I am not the only one who thinks this. —Words on a page We cut off the commissioner's head! We will cut off more! This rotten nation will fall! Victory shall be ours! Nika, Sonya... I fight for you. —Words on a page Zima and Gummy found a large pile of papers in the basement of the abandoned theater that served as the Ursus Student Self-Government Group's temporary base of operations. At first, she thought it was the script of a particularly incoherent play, but Absinthe's examination of municipal archives revealed that the basement had existed from before the theater was even built. It had been part of the prison system centuries ago, used to store and destroy the possessions of executed inmates. Zima began to examine the papers again. The inmates who wrote them had likely been put on death row for treason, suppressed and arrested by the enforcers of Ursus. Each sheet was subtly different from the others in texture or color, and each was written by a different hand. They mark the countless acts of resistance over the centuries, big and small. By farmers, poets, soldiers, and madmen. Their dates are often many years apart. Some wrote in factories driven by Originium External Combustion Engine, while others had only recently heard about that new invention. Ultimately, however, all their final letters ended up in the same dark corner. Zima tried to identify the writers, but unsurprisingly neither these 'rebellions' nor those who carried the flag of resistance had left their names upon the vast history of Ursus. The first thought I had might seem childish. I was thinking about how many Sonyas there have been over the centuries, how many Annas, Rosalinds, Natalyas, and Zoyas... how many Peters and Ivans. I felt a chill when I saw the name 'Sonya' on that piece of paper. Was it fate or coincidence that I came across it? I put down the papers and looked over the dust-covered basement, filled with history. This time, I thought, it would be different. I'd make sure it was different. —Operator Zima

[Classified Log]
Operator Zima's after-action report from their rescue of the student Rania mentioned various accidents in the course of the operation, such as a shadowy figure that flashed by the window at a secret meeting, or a schedule that went mysteriously missing from a locked cabinet. Even on the day of the operation, some students in charge of logistics were interrogated in the alleys by police with their epaulettes removed, as though there were eyes from up high seeing through all their plans, even if they had managed to pull wool over the eyes of the nobles at the hearing.
Zima emphasized, however, that all these accidents seemed to amount to nothing. Even the stamped warrant for their arrest seemed to have quietly disappeared. She initially thought it was the result of Rhodes Island's lobbying, expressing surprise at how we were able to take care of such matters, while still being unable to deliver long-range communications equipment.
As a matter of fact, Rhodes Island's activities in Ursus have encountered tremendous resistance ever since the Far North Incident, as though there were a pair of invisible eyes constantly watching our every move from atop Grypherburg.
The intentions of Ursus's regime remain unknown at this time, and establishing direct communications would be premature. In the wake of the ■■■■ Incident, we must reassess this ancient nation and its sprawling, convoluted organization.

Botani, also known as Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva, is a former student of the Imperial College of Science and Engineering in Grypherburg. After withdrawing from school, she joined Rhodes Island by Operator Zima's recommendation, continuing to study Originium communications while participating in field missions.

Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Botani shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.11u/L
Operator Botani demonstrates strong awareness of Oripathy prevention.

Operator Botani has 'modified' her right antler by embedding a metal antenna to improve her ability to receive communication signals. Medical examination indicates no harm has been done to the nervous system, but the damage at the connection point and potential cervical spine issues from the metallic materials require ongoing monitoring.

Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva is not the name Botani was born with, but it is the name that stayed with her the longest.
The award displayed on the wall, the fading photo framed in gemstone, and the thick stack of penalty decisions all bear witness to important moments in Tishinna's life.
For a long time, she thought she was lucky to be admitted to the Imperial College of Science and Engineering in Grypherburg under a generous scholarship from Grand Duchess Yelizaveta, even receiving an invitation to the Grand Duchess's solemn manor. Where, to her bewilderment, she was made to stand by the fireplace for an hour, watching the Grand Duchess speak to her advisers without being granted an audience, or even a single glance. It felt very cold outside when she left that building.
The Imperial College of Science and Engineering was also a far cry from what Tishinna had dreamed of. It was a garden of wealthy nobility, where the unruly children of aristocrats were sent to spend a few years, whereupon they became 'intellectuals'. There was no place there for a commoner from Bresk, and an Elafia at that. Indeed, there were hardly any non-Ursine students at the school. Tishinna often found herself locked out of her room at night, or having to search for her shoes and scarf early in the morning because they had mysteriously gone missing.
She eventually took up residence in a storage room at the library, which was open 24/7. This earned her the nickname 'Botani'—derived from 'botanik', or 'bookworm'—but also a place of peace and quiet. At the library, she found a notebook belonging to one Ksenia Markovna Nelidova, which seemed to be a survival guide from a non-Ursine student. Times had changed, and many of the locations and people in the notebook were no longer relevant, but Tishinna found courage in it nonetheless. Books had always been better teachers to her: following the guidance of professional textbooks, she created the communications device she had long sought, even modifying her own antler to hear signals from afar.
Then, everything changed one night.
The cries from the Far North drowned her. She tried to tell others what she heard, but found that she had no voice, and thus no power to bring about change. Listening to the voices from the Far North, she felt the pain of snowflakes cutting her skin open, and finally realized why the Grand Duchess had summoned her that day only to ignore her.
It was all so simple. It was the same reason she was admitted into this college for aristocrats: the Grand Duchess needed an example of her benevolence. All she needed from Tishinna was for her to be seen walking into the manor and spending an hour inside, so that the people would praise the kindness and benevolence of their Grand Duchess. What she thought had been the product of her hard work and good fortune was no more than a political show.
Since that night, Tishinna's name began to frequent the school's penalty notices, while the nickname 'Botani' she had been mocked with began to spread amongst the students trying to speak out for the tragedy in the far north.

Botani finally met Mantra and Raidian in Rhodes Island once things had settled down, even receiving a microphone autographed by Raidian. After learning that Team Mantra's members held open seminars on the effective use of long-range communications Arts, Botani could often be seen in Engineering's presentation room, hoping to sit in on one. I learned a lot from those seminars. It seemed like the attendees didn't know each other very well, sitting apart from each other. I don't have a very good memory for faces, so I didn't have the courage to greet unfamiliar colleagues either. In fact, I couldn't even tell who were supposed to be the lecturers and who were the students. Fortunately, that situation did not last for long. One day, the lecturers came to quiz me after I had just performed some repairs on my antenna. Their questions were quite difficult, and I saw the disappointment on their faces when I failed to answer one... After that, I began spending my nights studying in my room, trying to keep up with them. I suppose I did well enough, and I felt the benefit of this unique form of education. I learned a lot of new things. As far as surprises... I found there were far more lecturers than students at these seminars, and for some reason they all liked to question me. —Operator Botani I went to the Engineering Department's presentation room too. I thought the Team Mantra seminars were only a legend, but they turned out to be real! Botani didn't look like she liked to talk, so we only sat around, none of us daring to ask questions. Then one day, the antenna on her head quivered, and I realized it was a sign for us to ask questions, so I went up to her! Her Ursine accent left a deep impression on me. She spoke methodically at a careful pace, and whenever I asked a question lacking in rigor, she stopped to let me think for myself. I would have to go back to my room and think about it all night, then she would tell me the correct answer the following day. In a matter of weeks, the other new engineers and I felt we made significant progress in our technical and theoretical knowledge. We wrote a joint letter of appreciation to Mantra, thanking her for the help her team had given us. —An engineering operator So is that why no one came to the seminars?! Everyone went to the presentation room—I was waiting for them in the break room! Isn't it an Engineering tradition to discuss academic problems in the break room? Did I misunderstand something? Well, whatever, I'll just hide this letter before the captain finds out... She asked you to give it to me? She knew?! —Operator Elysium

Tishinna Viktorovna Belyaeva is the name Botani has used for the longest, but it is not the name she was born with.
Her original name came from the frost and springs of Sami, given to her by her sister, which she claims is untranslatable into any other language.
A shadow came over her eyes as she brought up her sister.
Her sister was not like her at all, not even like their mother. One day, her sister took her to see the ice springs, only to leave her alone in the snow-covered woods. She called her sister's name in panic and dug a shallow hole in the ground, trying to hide herself in it... She does not recall how long she spent in the dark woods, for her memory stopped there.
